literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在第29天,IVX-A12和RSVPreF3施用增加了RSV A中和抗体(nAb)水平,几何平均倍数上升(GMFR)分别为3.4和6.5,以及RSV B nAb水平,GMFR分别为2.9和5.4。IVX-A12(而非 RSVPreF3)也增加了 hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) 和 hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb 水平。 [10.1093/infdis/jiag531]

在1012名因急性呼吸道感染(ARI)住院的婴儿中,有655名患有下呼吸道疾病(LRTD),其中386名病例婴儿中有114名(30%)和269名对照婴儿中有171名(64%)出生于呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)preF疫苗接种的母亲。疫苗对RSV-LRTD住院的保护效果为77.8%(95%置信区间,66.4%-85.3%),在出生至6个月龄的婴儿中观察到更高的保护效果。 [10.1001/jamapediatrics.2026.3391]
RSV 抗原检测的敏感性范围为 20.6%(腺病毒)至 79.7%(hMPV),而所有六个目标的特异性均超过 99%。对于 RSV,抗原检测阳性率随病毒载量急剧增加,病毒载量≥10^6–10^7 拷贝/100 μL 时接近 90–100%,病毒载量≤10^4–10^5 拷贝/100 μL 时下降到 50% 以下。 [10.1128/jcm.00964-26]
该审查支持扩大对患有严重RSV疾病并进入第二个RSV季节的8至19个月婴儿和儿童RSV免疫的高风险标准。这表明对于这个特定年龄组需要有针对性的免疫策略的共识。 [10.1542/peds.2026-079047]

经过倾向评分匹配后,纳入了 52 740 名 IBD 患者和 104 997 名非 IBD 对照。219 名 IBD 患者和 426 名非 IBD 患者发生 RSV 感染。在我们研究期间的所有年份中,发病率 之间的 发病率 之间的 RSV 发生率相似。18.26% 的 IBD-RSV 患者因 RSV 相关住院,而非 IBD 患者则为 13.15% (P = .08)。两组均很少入住 ICU(<1%)。 [10.1093/ibd/izag103]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels. [10.1093/infdis/jiag531]

Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD), with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers. [10.1001/jamapediatrics.2026.3391]

RSV vaccines were associated with improved RSV-associated outcomes, with VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations at 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%), and varying by age and residency duration. [10.1001/jamainternmed.2026.3841]
Sensitivity of the antigen tests for RSV ranged from 20.6% (adenovirus) to 79.7% (hMPV), while specificity exceeded 99% for all six targets. [10.1128/jcm.00964-26]

The review supports expanding the high-risk criteria for RSV immunization in infants and children aged 8 through 19 months who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. This indicates a consensus on the need for targeted immunization strategies in this specific age group. [10.1542/peds.2026-079047]

news.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 疾病预防控制中心发表了一篇题为“随着时间的推移疾病水平|呼吸系统疾病讨论呼吸系统疾病,包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)。 [news-4265ae8716946c8a]
据韩国疾病控制和预防中心报告,老年人口 RSV 住院人数增加,患者年龄构成发生显着变化。 [news-0ca3bf28f0b28c81]
CIDRAP 发表的一项研究发现,与没有 UMC 的儿童相比,患有 RSV 住院的患有基础疾病 (UMC) 的儿童的医疗费用明显更高。该研究描述了在这些人群中使用单克隆抗体的成本效益。 [news-c3c763ded091a2ff]
韩国的一些产后护理中心需要RSV 疫苗接种才能入院,济州岛的一家产后护理中心于2026年9月出现RSV感染暴发,导致暂时关闭。韩国疾病管理本部报告称,去年产后护理中心发生 22 例 RSV 群感染,创历史新高,今年上半年则有 15 例。 [news-ab4ade8405097539]
该文章重点介绍了早期流感季节和晚期呼吸道合胞病毒季节,强调感染预防人员需要监测这些趋势。它还讨论了各种与医疗保健相关的主题,包括使用实时定位系统 (RTLS) 进行手部卫生、马拉维艾滋病毒计划以及法国首例沙蒙达病毒人类病例。 [news-bf210916ca2c8a5e]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Respiratory syncytial virus news developments.
key_findings_en: The CDC published an article titled 'Illness Levels Over Time | Respiratory Illnesses' discussing respiratory illnesses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). [news-4265ae8716946c8a]

An increase in RSV hospitalizations among the elderly population, with a significant shift in the age composition of patients, reported by the Korea Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. [news-0ca3bf28f0b28c81]

A study published by CIDRAP found that children with underlying medical conditions (UMCs) hospitalized with RSV had significantly higher medical costs compared to those without UMCs. The study described the cost-benefits of monoclonal antibody use in these populations. [news-c3c763ded091a2ff]

Some postpartum care centers in Korea require RSV vaccination for admission, and a postpartum care center in Jeju had an outbreak of RSV infection in September 2026, leading to temporary closure. [news-ab4ade8405097539]
The article highlights the early flu season and late RSV season, emphasizing the need for infection preventionists to monitor these trends. [news-bf210916ca2c8a5e]

brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following Respiratory syncytial virus news developments.
The CDC published an article titled 'Illness Levels Over Time | Respiratory Illnesses' discussing respiratory illnesses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). [news-4265ae8716946c8a].

An increase in RSV hospitalizations among the elderly population, with a significant shift in the age composition of patients, reported by the Korea Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. [news-0ca3bf28f0b28c81].
A study published by CIDRAP found that children with underlying medical conditions (UMCs) hospitalized with RSV had significantly higher medical costs compared to those without UMCs.

Some postpartum care centers in Korea require RSV vaccination for admission, and a postpartum care center in Jeju had an outbreak of RSV infection in September 2026, leading to temporary closure. [news-ab4ade8405097539].
news.zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。；疾病预防控制中心发表了一篇题为“随着时间的推移疾病水平|呼吸系统疾病讨论呼吸系统疾病,包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)。 [news-4265ae8716946c8a]。；据韩国疾病控制和预防中心报告,老年人口 RSV 住院人数增加,患者年龄构成发生显着变化。 [news-0ca3bf28f0b28c81]。；CIDRAP 发表的一项研究发现,与没有 UMC 的儿童相比,患有 RSV 住院的患有基础疾病 (UMC) 的儿童的医疗费用明显更高。该研究描述了在这些人群中使用单克隆抗体的成本效益。 [news-c3c763ded091a2ff]。；韩国的一些产后护理中心需要RSV 疫苗接种才能入院,济州岛的一家产后护理中心于2026年9月出现RSV感染暴发,导致暂时关闭。韩国疾病管理本部报告称,去年产后护理中心发生 22 例 RSV 群感染,创历史新高,今年上半年则有 15 例。

papers.title: Maternal RSVpreF Vaccine Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Hospitalized Infants.
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: In February 2025, Australia introduced maternal vaccination with bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in the National Immunization Program for pregnant individuals from 28 weeks' gestation as the primary, year-round strategy to prevent RSV disease in infants 6 months of age or younger. OBJECTIVE: To estimate effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. EXPOSURE: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks' gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to estimate the effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia, following the introduction of the vaccine in the National Immunization Program in February 2025.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia, involving infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with acute respiratory illness (ARI) at 6 months of age or younger, from March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026.
analysis.methods: Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%, with data analyzed from March 2026 through May 2026.
analysis.main_results: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD), with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, with higher effectiveness observed in younger age groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger, with the highest effectiveness observed in the earliest age intervals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide cautious evidence for the effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination in preventing RSV hospitalization in young infants, which could inform future vaccination strategies and public health recommendations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design, which may introduce bias, and the evidence is limited by the sample size, with future analyses needed to evaluate effectiveness among additional subgroups.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination against RSV hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in Australia. The retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted across 9 hospitals, analyzing data from March 2025 to February 2026. Results showed vaccine effectiveness (VE) against RSV lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) hospitalization at 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, with higher effectiveness observed in younger infants. The authors concluded that the vaccine demonstrated high year-round effectiveness, particularly in the earliest age intervals. However, the study's design and sample size limit the confidence in these findings, and future analyses with larger samples are needed to confirm effectiveness in additional subgroups.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to estimate the effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia, following the introduction of the vaccine in the National Immunization Program in February 2025.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia, involving infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with acute respiratory illness (ARI) at 6 months of age or younger, from March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026.
elements_en.methods: Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%, with data analyzed from March 2026 through May 2026.
elements_en.main_results: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD), with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, with higher effectiveness observed in younger age groups.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger, with the highest effectiveness observed in the earliest age intervals.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide cautious evidence for the effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination in preventing RSV hospitalization in young infants, which could inform future vaccination strategies and public health recommendations.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design, which may introduce bias, and the evidence is limited by the sample size, with future analyses needed to evaluate effectiveness among additional subgroups.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项采用测试阴性设计的回顾性病例对照研究在澳大利亚9家医院进行,研究对象为2025年3月1日至2026年2月28日期间妊娠28周出生、6个月以下因急性呼吸道疾病(ARI)住院的婴儿。
elements_zh.methods: 使用混杂因素调整的逻辑回归将 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 计算为(1 - 调整后的比值比)× 100%,数据分析时间为 2026 年 3 月至 2026 年 5 月。
elements_zh.main_results: 在1012名因急性呼吸道感染(ARI)住院的婴儿中,有655名患有下呼吸道疾病(LRTD),其中386名病例婴儿中有114名(30%)和269名对照婴儿中有171名(64%)出生于呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)preF疫苗接种的母亲。疫苗对RSV-LRTD住院的保护效果为77.8%(95%置信区间,66.4%-85.3%),在出生至6个月龄的婴儿中观察到更高的保护效果。

papers.title_zh: 母亲 RSVpreF 疫苗 对住院婴儿中 呼吸道合胞病毒 的有效性。
papers.source_body_en: IMPORTANCE: In February 2025, Australia introduced maternal vaccination with bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in the National Immunization Program for pregnant individuals from 28 weeks' gestation as the primary, year-round strategy to prevent RSV disease in infants 6 months of age or younger. OBJECTIVE: To estimate effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. EXPOSURE: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks' gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

papers.title: Recommendations for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease in Infants and Children: Policy Statement.
papers.abstract: This policy statement updates recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) for the use of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization for the prevention of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) caused by RSV in infants and children. The AAP recommends RSV immunization for all infants under 8 months of age born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of their pregnant parent; and for infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. A review of evidence supports expanding the high-risk criteria for administration of RSV immunization in infants and children 8 through 19 months of age entering their second RSV season. A discussion of the evidence supporting the AAP recommendations and additional details on infants and children included in the expanded recommendations are in the accompanying technical report (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079049).

papers.title_zh: 预防婴儿和儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 疾病的建议:政策声明。
papers.source_body_en: This policy statement updates recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) for the use of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization for the prevention of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) caused by RSV in infants and children. The AAP recommends RSV immunization for all infants under 8 months of age born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of their pregnant parent; and for infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. A review of evidence supports expanding the high-risk criteria for administration of RSV immunization in infants and children 8 through 19 months of age entering their second RSV season. A discussion of the evidence supporting the AAP recommendations and additional details on infants and children included in the expanded recommendations are in the accompanying technical report (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079049).

papers.title: A Phase 2 Trial of a Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Metapneumovirus Combination Virus-Like Particle Vaccine IVX-A12 in Adults ≥60 Years of Age.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Older adults (≥60 years) are susceptible to severe outcomes from infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or human metapneumovirus (hMPV). IVX-A12 is an investigational vaccine that uses virus-like particles (VLPs) to elicit an immune response against RSV and hMPV. Methods This Phase 2 trial (NCT06481579) randomized (1:1) adults ≥60 years of age to receive a single dose of IVX-A12 (150 μg RSV/150 μg hMPV) or the licensed RSV vaccine RSVPreF3 120 μg with AS01E adjuvant. Safety and immunogenicity were evaluated through 180 days post-vaccination. Results Overall, 143 participants received IVX-A12 (n = 71) or RSVPreF3 (n = 72). Solicited adverse reactions were reported through 7 days post-vaccination (IVX-A12, 25 [35.2%]; RSVPreF3, 36 [50.0%]). Unsolicited adverse events (AEs) were collected through Day 29 (IVX-A12, 5 [7.0%]; RSVPreF3, 11 [15.3%]). Serious AEs (IVX-A12, 2 [2.8%]; RSVPreF3, 1 [1.4%]) and medically attended AEs (IVX-A12, 1 [1.4%]; RSVPreF3, 9 [12.5%]) were documented through Day 181. There were no AEs of special interest and AEs leading to study discontinuation. At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels. Conclusions IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and elicited nAb responses against their targeted pathogens. Given the neutralizing antibody response following IVX-A12, further investigation of an RSV-hMPV VLP combination vaccine is warranted.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Older adults (≥60 years) are susceptible to severe outcomes from infection with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or human metapneumovirus (hMPV). IVX-A12 is an investigational vaccine that uses virus-like particles (VLPs) to elicit an immune response against RSV and hMPV. Methods This Phase 2 trial (NCT06481579) randomized (1:1) adults ≥60 years of age to receive a single dose of IVX-A12 (150 μg RSV/150 μg hMPV) or the licensed RSV vaccine RSVPreF3 120 μg with AS01E adjuvant. Safety and immunogenicity were evaluated through 180 days post-vaccination. Results Overall, 143 participants received IVX-A12 (n = 71) or RSVPreF3 (n = 72). Solicited adverse reactions were reported through 7 days post-vaccination (IVX-A12, 25 [35.2%]; RSVPreF3, 36 [50.0%]). Unsolicited adverse events (AEs) were collected through Day 29 (IVX-A12, 5 [7.0%]; RSVPreF3, 11 [15.3%]). Serious AEs (IVX-A12, 2 [2.8%]; RSVPreF3, 1 [1.4%]) and medically attended AEs (IVX-A12, 1 [1.4%]; RSVPreF3, 9 [12.5%]) were documented through Day 181. There were no AEs of special interest and AEs leading to study discontinuation. At Day 29, IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 administration increased RSV A neutralizing antibody (nAb) levels with geometric mean fold rise (GMFR) of 3.4 and 6.5, and RSV B nAb levels with GMFR of 2.9 and 5.4, respectively. IVX-A12, but not RSVPreF3, also increased hMPV A (GMFR 3.0) and hMPV B (GMFR 2.9) nAb levels. Conclusions IVX-A12 and RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and elicited nAb responses against their targeted pathogens. Given the neutralizing antibody response following IVX-A12, further investigation of an RSV-hMPV VLP combination vaccine is warranted.

papers.title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

papers.title_zh: 2019-2023 年悉尼儿童医院网络收治的幼儿的增强型 呼吸道合胞病毒 监测。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare Beneficiaries Residing in Nursing Homes.
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates are needed to determine the effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccinations during their first season of availability among populations at high risk for severe RSV. OBJECTIVE: To assess RSV VE against RSV-associated outcomes for nursing home residents. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries used electronic medical claims data from September 10, 2023, to March 30, 2024. A cohort was created for each outcome: an RSV-associated hospitalization cohort; an RSV-associated death cohort; a severe RSV-associated outcome cohort; and an RSV-associated thromboembolic event cohort. To be eligible for inclusion in a cohort, a Medicare fee-for-service beneficiary must be aged 65 years or older, reside in a US nursing home during the study period for at least 1 day, have continuous enrollment in Medicare Parts A and B (365 days prior to the index date), and have continuous enrollment in Part D (beginning on June 21, 2023). EXPOSURE: RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes were RSV-associated hospitalization, RSV-associated death, severe RSV-associated outcomes (intensive care unit or critical care unit admission, medical ventilator use, or RSV-associated death), and RSV-associated thromboembolic event. RSV diagnoses and outcome definitions were based on claims with relevant International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes. RSV vaccine doses were determined from Medicare Part D claims using the National Drug Code Directory. Hazard ratios (HRs) from multivariable Cox proportional hazards models compared the times to first outcomes among RSV vaccinated beneficiaries and unvaccinated beneficiaries. VE was calculated as (1-HR) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%). Among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years VE was 60% (95% CI, 35%-76%), 75% (95% CI, 67%-82%) among beneficiaries 75 years or older, 67% (95% CI, 55%-76%) among short-stay residents (<100 cumulative days), and 80% (95% CI, 68%-87%) among long-stay residents (≥100 cumulative days). VE against RSV-associated death was 56% (95% CI, 39%-69%), VE against severe RSV-associated outcomes was 59% (95% CI, 44%-70%), and VE against RSV-associated thromboembolic events was 66% (95% CI, 44%-79%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, in the first season of availability, RSV vaccines were associated with improved RSV-associated outcomes among US Medicare beneficiaries residing in nursing homes.

papers.title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to share lessons from the rapid implementation of RSV prevention products and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. The research was needed to address the challenge of integrating new RSV prevention strategies into routine clinical practice.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable monoclonal antibody nirsevimab in two maternity hospitals within the Sydney Local Health District. The study period spanned from February to September 2025, focusing on immunisation uptake among mothers and eligible newborns.
analysis.methods: Deidentified summary data from electronic medical records were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used to evaluate the rollout process and identify factors influencing immunisation uptake.
analysis.main_results: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in the two hospitals increased from 4% in the first month of rollout to 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reasons for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that coordinated engagement with multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for successful program rollout. The study highlights the importance of clear messaging and systemic safeguards in implementing multiple immunisation products for distinct groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of future RSV prevention programs by demonstrating the effectiveness of strategies such as clinician education and integration of immunisation into medical record workflows. They also provide insights into improving uptake and reducing refusal rates for RSV vaccines and monoclonal antibodies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on deidentified summary data and the absence of recorded reasons for refusal. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the descriptive nature of the analysis and the lack of detailed statistical or causal interpretations.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, including the maternal vaccine and the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab, in two maternity hospitals in Sydney, Australia. It reports that RSV vaccination coverage among mothers improved significantly from 4% in February 2025 to 70-74% by September 2025. As coverage increased, fewer newborns required nirsevimab. However, 36% of eligible families declined the antibody, with no recorded reasons. The study highlights the importance of multidisciplinary engagement and clear messaging in program implementation. It also notes that integrating immunisation into medical record workflows can support program adoption. The findings suggest that while the rollout was successful, the lack of detailed refusal data and the descriptive nature of the analysis limit the strength of the evidence. These insights can inform future RSV prevention strategies and improve immunisation uptake.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分享快速实施 RSV 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。这项研究需要解决将新的 RSV 预防策略纳入常规临床实践的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及在悉尼地方卫生区的两家妇产医院推出 RSV 母体 疫苗 和可注射单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗。该研究时间跨度为 2025 年 2 月至 9 月,重点关注母亲和符合条件的新生儿的免疫接种情况。
elements_zh.methods: 来自电子病历的去识别化摘要数据被描述性地分析为计数和比例。实施研究综合框架用于评估推广过程并确定影响免疫接种的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV 疫苗接种 在两家医院分娩的妇女的覆盖率从推出第一个月的 4% 增加到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,拒绝的原因没有记录。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明多学科领导者和临床医生的协调参与对于项目的成功推出至关重要。该研究强调了在针对不同群体实施多种免疫产品时,明确的信息传递和系统保障措施的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过证明临床医生教育和将免疫接种纳入医疗记录工作流程等策略的有效性,为未来 RSV 预防计划的发展提供信息。他们还提供了有关提高 RSV 疫苗 和单克隆抗体的吸收率和降低拒绝率的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于它依赖于未识别身份的汇总数据,并且没有记录拒绝的原因。由于分析的描述性以及缺乏详细的统计或因果解释,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Respiratory syncytial virus incidence and clinical outcomes in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: a National Veterans Affairs cohort study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Data describing the incidence and clinical outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are limited. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database. Adults with IBD were identified using a previously validated algorithm and matched 1:2 to non-IBD controls using propensity score matching. Laboratory-confirmed RSV infections that occurred between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2024, were identified using standardized laboratory codes and confirmed by manual chart adjudication. Primary outcomes included RSV incidence and hospitalizations. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) admission and patient outcomes stratified by IBD medication class. RESULTS: After propensity score matching, 52 740 IBD patients and 104 997 non-IBD controls were included. Infection with RSV occurred in 219 patients with IBD and 426 non-IBD patients. Incidence rates of RSV were similar between cohorts across all years in our study period. Hospitalization related to RSV occurred in 18.26% of IBD-RSV patients compared with 13.15% of non-IBD patients (P = .08). ICU admission was rare in both groups (<1%). Among patients with IBD, RSV-related hospitalization did not differ significantly by medication class, when comparing biologic therapy (8.93%) with 5-aminosalicylic acid monotherapy (17.58%) (P = .15). CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, patients with IBD, with predominantly lower exposure to advanced therapies, did not have higher rates of RSV infection or worse clinical outcomes compared with matched non-IBD controls. RSV outcomes were similar across IBD medication classes. These findings support current vaccination recommendations and provide reassurance regarding RSV risk among patients with IBD.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the incidence and clinical outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). A nationwide retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database, where adults with IBD were matched 1:2 to non-IBD controls. The study identified RSV infections between 2021 and 2024 and assessed outcomes such as hospitalization and ICU admission. Results showed similar RSV incidence rates between IBD and non-IBD patients, with no significant difference in hospitalization rates. The findings suggest that IBD patients do not have higher RSV infection rates or worse clinical outcomes compared to non-IBD controls, and outcomes were consistent across different IBD medication classes. These results support existing vaccination recommendations and offer reassurance about RSV risk in IBD patients. The study's evidence is strong, but specific limitations were not detailed.

papers.title: Circulating Biomarkers Associated with Severe Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Infants Under 2 Years: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in infants, but circulating biomarkers for severity stratification remain insufficiently validated. This systematic review evaluated circulating biomarkers associated with acute RSV disease severity in children aged≤ 24 months. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for English-language reports published between 1 January 2016 and 1 March 2026, with the last searches performed on 1 March 2026. Study-level risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, according to study design. Findings were synthesized descriptively using study-level effect estimates and reported severity-discrimination measures. Twenty-four studies contributed 174 extractable comparisons. Biomarker associations varied across populations, age strata, sampling times, and severity definitions, and reproducibility across independent cohorts was limited. In one cohort, fibrinogen and the fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) showed large differences between severity groups; FAR had a reported AUC of 0.875. These findings do not establish comparative superiority or external validity. Important limitations include heterogeneous clinical comparisons, limited confounder adjustment, and predominantly single-cohort evidence. Current evidence does not support using FAR, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), or other circulating biomarkers alone to predict subsequent clinical deterioration. Whether these markers add useful information to clinical assessment requires prospective validation. Registration: PROSPERO, CRD420261471336.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates circulating biomarkers associated with severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants under 2 years. The review included 24 studies contributing 174 extractable comparisons, with evidence sourced from PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus between 2016 and 2026. The findings show variability in biomarker associations across populations, age groups, sampling times, and severity definitions, with limited reproducibility across independent cohorts. The fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) demonstrated a reported AUC of 0.875 in one cohort, but the evidence does not establish its comparative superiority or external validity. The review highlights the need for prospective validation to determine if these markers add value to clinical assessment and cautions against using them alone to predict clinical deterioration. The study-level risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale or the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and the review was registered with PROSPERO.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因,但用于严重程度分层的循环生物标志物仍未得到充分验证。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本系统评价评估了 24 个月以下儿童中与急性 RSV 疾病严重程度相关的循环生物标志物。PubMed、Web of Science 和 Scopus 搜索了 2016 年 1 月 1 日至 2026 年 3 月 1 日之间发表的英文报告,最后一次搜索于 2026 年 3 月 1 日进行。根据研究设计,使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华量表或乔安娜·布里格斯研究所检查表评估研究层面的偏倚风险。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 使用研究水平的效果估计和报告的严重性歧视措施对研究结果进行描述性综合。在一项 队列研究 中,纤维蛋白原和纤维蛋白原与白蛋白的比率 (FAR) 在严重程度组之间显示出巨大差异;FAR 的 AUC 报告为 0.875。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 生物标志物关联因人群、年龄层、采样时间和严重程度定义而异,并且独立 队列研究 的再现性有限。重要的局限性包括异质性临床比较、有限的混杂因素调整以及主要是单一的 队列研究 证据。这些发现并未确立比较优势或外部有效性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 这些标志物是否为临床评估添加有用的信息需要前瞻性验证。目前的证据不支持单独使用 FAR、中性粒细胞与淋巴细胞比率 (NLR) 或其他循环生物标志物来预测随后的临床恶化。

papers.title: Phosphate-modified PROTECs as potent antivirals against respiratory syncytial virus by targeting the fusion protein.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of severe respiratory infections, highlighting the need for antiviral strategies with novel mechanisms. Here, we extended our protein-radical-oxidation targeting enediyne chimera (PROTEC) strategy to the RSV fusion (F) protein. BMS-433771 was employed as the protein-targeting group and conjugated to a maleimide-based acyclic enediyne bearing phosphate hydrophilicity-adjusting groups, which simplified synthesis compared with our previous sulfate-containing PROTECs. Three analogues with different linker lengths ( n = 3, 5, and 7) were synthesized and evaluated. All compounds showed low cytotoxicity (CC 50 > 100 μM) and potent anti-RSV activity. PROTEC-R7 ( n = 7) exhibited the highest potency, with an IC 50 of 110.3 nM and a selectivity index > 906. In contrast, the non-targeted control EDY-R showed substantially weaker activity (IC 50 = 16.3 μM). These results demonstrate the importance of targeted delivery and linker engineering and support PROTEC as a promising strategy for targeting viral surface proteins.

papers.title: In Vitro Evaluation of Repurposed Antivirals and Their Combinations Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Human Parainfluenza Virus Type 2: Evidence of Ribavirin-Oseltamivir Synergy.
papers.abstract: Treating respiratory viral infections remains challenging, necessitating exploration of novel therapeutic approaches. Alternative strategies, such as drug repurposing or combinations, are essential for treating them. This study evaluated the in vitro activities of the antivirals ribavirin, favipiravir, and oseltamivir, and the mucolytic drugs N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and erdosteine, alone or in combination, against Human Parainfluenza Virus (HPIV) and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). HPIV-2 and RSV were cultured in VERO and HEp-2 cell lines, respectively. Antiviral efficacy was assessed by calculating IC 50 values using MTT and plaque reduction assays. For combination studies, synergy scores were analyzed using the SynergyFinder program. We investigated potential interactions underlying the synergistic activities using an in silico approach, that combined virtual screening and molecular docking. The IC 50 values of ribavirin, favipiravir, and oseltamivir against HPIV-2 and RSV ranged from 4.46 to 14.1 μg/mL, and the results from both methods were highly similar. All three antivirals' cytotoxicity was well above their C-max, and SIs were 12.43-36.69 for HPIV-2 and 15.88-38.12 for RSV. The ribavirin-oseltamivir combination synergy scores of 13.35 for HPIV-2 and 17.98 for RSV indicate clear synergism, while other combinations were additive. Docking analysis identified potential molecular interactions that may contribute to the antiviral activity of the ribavirin-oseltamivir combination against RSV and HPIV-2. Ribavirin, favipiravir, and oseltamivir showed good activity against HPIV-2 and RSV, and the ribavirin-oseltamivir combination exhibited strong synergistic interactions, suggesting promising therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Recommendations for the Prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Disease in Infants and Children: Technical Report.
papers.abstract: This technical report accompanies the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) policy statement (https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2026-079047) and recommendations for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization during the 2026-2027 RSV season. The rationale is presented for recommending immunization of all infants younger than 8 months born during or entering their first RSV season, unless the infant has documented protection from vaccination of the pregnant parent; and infants and children 8 through 19 months of age who are at high risk of severe RSV disease and entering their second RSV season. The report synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology, disease burden, immunization effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness in pediatric populations; including evidence supporting expansion of high-risk groups for second season administration. Additionally, the report provides an overview of available RSV immunization products, formulations, and coadministration with other immunizations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本报告解决了针对婴儿和儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疾病更新预防策略的需求,重点关注 2026-2027 RSV 季节期间免疫建议的基本原理。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一份技术报告,综合了儿科人群(包括患有严重 RSV 疾病的高风险人群)的 RSV 流行病学、疾病负担、免疫有效性、安全性和成本效益的当前证据。
elements_zh.methods: 该报告回顾并综合了 RSV 免疫的现有证据,包括有效性、安全性和成本效益的数据,并概述了可用的 RSV 免疫产品和配方。
elements_zh.main_results: 该报告概述了建议对在第一个 RSV 季节期间或进入其第一个 RSV 季节期间出生的所有 8 个月以下婴儿进行免疫接种的理由,除非婴儿已证明怀孕父母对 疫苗接种 具有保护作用,以及患有严重 RSV 疾病高风险并进入第二个 RSV 季节的 8 至 19 个月大的婴儿和儿童。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为支持扩大第二季 RSV 免疫接种的高危人群,这代表了解决弱势儿科人群疾病负担的一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 RSV 预防的公共卫生策略提供信息,特别是在识别高危人群和优化婴儿和儿童的免疫计划方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该报告基于现有证据的综合,这些证据在普遍性和最新数据方面可能存在局限性,但证据被认为是强有力的,并且对所提供的建议得到了充分支持。

papers.title: Dynamic structural adaptation of a conserved interaction hotspot in the respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F.
papers.abstract: Protein interaction sites must maintain structural integrity while accommodating conformational fluctuations and sequence perturbations. Molecular determinants that distinguish locally adaptable residues from structurally constrained positions within conserved interfaces remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate this problem using the prefusion respiratory syncytial virus fusion glycoprotein F as a model system, focusing on a conserved interaction hotspot proximal to the MEDI8897-binding interface. An integrated computational framework combining evolutionary conservation, structure-based energetic analysis, residue interaction networks, and molecular dynamics simulations was used to characterize mutation-dependent structural responses. Analysis of 1848 RSV F sequences revealed strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot comprising C69, P205, I206, N208, K209, and C212. Despite conservation, saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed pronounced heterogeneity in calculated energetic response to substitution. P205R and N208R produced highly unfavorable calculated energetic effects, whereas I206R exhibited an approximately neutral energetic response. Residue interaction network analysis identified I206 as topologically central residue with the highest betweenness and closeness centrality within the hotspot. Aggregate MD sampling comprised three independent 500-ns simulations for each of seven systems, yielding 10.5 μs of total simulation time. All systems retained the overall prefusion architecture over the simulated timescale but exhibited distinct local and interprotomer responses. N208R produced the strongest local perturbation, including increased hotspot flexibility and reduced interprotomer contact occupancy. In contrast, P205R maintained restrained local dynamics despite its energetic penalty, whereas I206R preserved a broadly wild-type-like dynamic profile. These findings indicate that energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics provide complementary information for characterizing mutation-induced structural adaptation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how protein interaction sites maintain structural integrity while allowing conformational changes and sequence variations. The research addressed a gap in knowledge about the molecular factors that differentiate adaptable residues from structurally constrained ones in conserved viral interfaces.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion glycoprotein F, specifically examining a conserved interaction hotspot near the MEDI8897-binding interface. It analyzed 1848 RSV F sequences to identify patterns of conservation and mutation effects.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed an integrated computational framework that combined evolutionary conservation analysis, structure-based energetic calculations, residue interaction network assessments, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate mutation-dependent structural responses.
analysis.main_results: Analysis of RSV F sequences showed strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot, including residues C69, P205, I206, N208, K209, and C212. Saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed significant variation in the energetic response to substitutions, with P205R and N208R showing highly unfavorable effects and I206R having a neutral response.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics provide distinct yet complementary insights into how mutations affect structural adaptation in viral proteins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results contribute to understanding the structural resilience of RSV proteins, which could inform the development of more effective antiviral strategies, including drug design and vaccine targeting.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on computational models and sequence analysis, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics. However, the use of a large dataset and multiple simulation approaches provides moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural adaptation of a conserved interaction hotspot in the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion glycoprotein F. The research aimed to understand how residues within this hotspot maintain structural integrity despite conformational changes and sequence variations. Using an integrated computational framework, the study analyzed 1848 RSV F sequences and found strong conservation of the CPINKC hotspot. Saturation mutagenesis and structural analysis revealed that substitutions at specific residues, such as P205R and N208R, had highly unfavorable energetic effects, while I206R showed a neutral response. The findings highlight the importance of energetic cost, residue interaction topology, and conformational dynamics in characterizing mutation-induced structural changes. These insights could inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting RSV. However, the study's reliance on computational models and sequence data limits the confidence in its conclusions, suggesting a moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解蛋白质相互作用位点如何保持结构完整性,同时允许构象变化和序列变化。该研究解决了关于区分保守病毒界面中适应性残基和结构受限残基的分子因素的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 融合糖蛋白 F,特别检查 MEDI8897 结合界面附近的保守相互作用热点。它分析了 1848 个 RSV F 序列,以确定保守模式和 突变 效应。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员采用了一个集成的计算框架,结合了进化守恒分析、基于结构的能量计算、残基相互作用网络评估和分子动力学模拟来评估依赖于 突变 的结构响应。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV F 序列分析显示 CPINKC 热点具有很强的保守性,包括残基 C69、P205、I206、N208、K209 和 C212。饱和诱变和结构分析揭示了对取代的能量反应的显着变化,其中P205R和N208R显示出高度不利的影响,而I206R具有中性反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,能量成本、残基相互作用拓扑和构象动力学为 突变 如何影响病毒蛋白的结构适应提供了独特但互补的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于了解 RSV 蛋白的结构弹性,这可以为开发更有效的 抗病毒药物 策略提供信息,包括药物设计和 疫苗 靶向。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于计算模型和序列分析,可能无法完全捕捉体内动态。然而,大型数据集和多种模拟方法的使用为结论提供了适度的可信度。

papers.abstract_zh: 蛋白质相互作用位点必须保持结构完整性,同时适应构象波动和序列扰动。将局部适应性残基与保守界面内结构受限位置区分开来的分子决定因素仍不完全清楚。在这里,我们使用预融合 呼吸道合胞病毒 融合糖蛋白 F 作为模型系统来研究这个问题,重点关注靠近 MEDI8897 结合界面的保守相互作用热点。使用结合了进化守恒、基于结构的能量分析、残基相互作用网络和分子动力学模拟的集成计算框架来表征依赖于 突变 的结构响应。对 1848 个 RSV F 序列的分析揭示了 CPINKC 热点(包括 C69、P205、I206、N208、K209 和 C212)的高度保守性。尽管保守,饱和诱变和结构分析揭示了计算的替代能量响应中明显的异质性。P205R 和 N208R 产生了非常不利的计算能量效应,而 I206R 表现出近似中性的能量响应。残基相互作用网络分析将 I206 确定为拓扑中心残基,在热点内具有最高的中介性和接近中心性。聚合 MD 采样包括七个系统中每个系统的三个独立的 500 ns 模拟,产生 10.5 μs 的总模拟时间。所有系统在模拟时间尺度上都保留了整体预融合架构,但表现出不同的局部和原体间响应。N208R 产生最强的局部扰动,包括增加热点灵活性和减少原体间接触占用。相比之下,P205R 尽管存在能量损失,但仍保持有限的局部动态,而 I206R 则保留了大致与野生型相似的动态特征。这些发现表明能量成本、残基相互作用拓扑和构象动力学为表征 突变 诱导的结构适应提供了补充信息。

papers.title: Respiratory Pathogens Detected among Pediatric Hospitalizations for Pneumonia: A Multicenter Study from Saitama, Japan.
papers.abstract: Routine in-hospital testing may not detect the full range of respiratory pathogens in children hospitalized with pneumonia. We conducted a prefecture-wide multicenter retrospective cohort study at four hospitals in Saitama, Japan, from July 2023 to March 2024 to describe detected respiratory pathogens and assess the additional findings obtained by multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) beyond routine in-hospital testing. Among 1,170 pediatric hospitalizations for acute respiratory infections (ARIs), 457 (39.1%) were complicated by pneumonia. Human metapneumovirus (hMPV; n=124, 27.1%) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; n=85, 18.6%) were the most frequently detected pathogens. Multiplex PCR was performed in 199 hospitalizations. Among 123 hospitalizations in which at least one in-hospital respiratory pathogen test was performed and all results were negative, multiplex PCR detected at least one pathogen in 85 (69.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted comparison excluding 16 group A Streptococcus-positive hospitalizations, antibiotic initiation was associated with older age, higher C-reactive protein levels, and absence of a positive in-hospital test. Among 210 antibiotic-treated hospitalizations without a positive in-hospital test, 110 underwent multiplex PCR and a viral pathogen was detected in 74/110 (67.3%). Multiplex PCR frequently identified pathogens after negative routine testing and broadened the detectable pathogen spectrum beyond targeted in-hospital tests.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A prefecture-wide multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at four hospitals in Saitama, Japan, from July 2023 to March 2024, involving 1,170 pediatric hospitalizations for acute respiratory infections (ARIs), of which 457 were complicated by pneumonia.
analysis.methods: Multiplex PCR was performed in 199 hospitalizations, and it frequently identified pathogens after negative routine testing, broadening the detectable pathogen spectrum beyond targeted in-hospital tests.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that multiplex PCR significantly enhances pathogen detection beyond routine testing, highlighting its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy in pediatric pneumonia cases.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the utility of multiplex PCR in detecting respiratory pathogens in children hospitalized with pneumonia in Saitama, Japan. The research aimed to assess whether multiplex PCR could identify pathogens beyond routine testing. Conducted at four hospitals between July 2023 and March 2024, the study included 1,170 pediatric hospitalizations for acute respiratory infections, of which 457 were complicated by pneumonia. Multiplex PCR was performed in 199 hospitalizations and detected pathogens in 69.1% of cases where routine testing was negative. In 210 antibiotic-treated hospitalizations without a positive routine test, 67.3% had a viral pathogen identified by multiplex PCR. The authors interpreted that multiplex PCR significantly improves pathogen detection, which could enhance diagnostic accuracy. The findings suggest that multiplex PCR may be valuable for more comprehensive pathogen identification in pediatric pneumonia cases. The study's retrospective design and potential for selection bias limit its evidence strength, though the large sample size and validated method support its conclusions.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,多重 PCR 可以提供更全面的病原体检测,这可能为改进小儿肺炎的诊断策略和有针对性的 治疗 方法提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的选择偏倚而受到限制,但由于样本量大且使用了经过验证的多重 PCR 方法,因此证据充足。

analysis_zh.main_results: 在 123 例院内呼吸道病原体检测呈阴性的住院患者中,多重 PCR 在 85 例患者中检测到至少一种病原体(69.1%)。此外,在 210 例接受抗生素治疗且院内检测未呈阳性的住院患者中,74/110 例 (67.3%) 通过多重 PCR 检测到病毒病原体。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,多重 PCR 显着增强了常规检测之外的病原体检测,突显了其提高小儿肺炎病例诊断准确性的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,多重 PCR 可以提供更全面的病原体检测,这可能为改进小儿肺炎的诊断策略和有针对性的 治疗 方法提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和潜在的选择偏倚而受到限制,但由于样本量大且使用了经过验证的多重 PCR 方法,因此证据充足。

papers.title: The MSC–RSV/HMPV interface: impacts on pulmonary homeostasis, remodeling, and risk of non-atopic asthma and COPD
papers.abstract: Respiratory tract infections continue to represent a major cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality. Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) are highlighted as key etiologic agents of bronchiolitis and pneumonia, particularly in children under two years old. Recurrent infections during the second year of life may be associated with significant histopathological damage and might also be a risk factor for developing chronic pulmonary diseases, such as non-atopic asthma. In adults, these viruses similarly elevate clinical burden on the elderly and individuals with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), causing the exacerbation of respiratory signals and symptoms and, consequently, promoting a chronic inflammatory response that modifies the lung tissue and disease progression. Tissue repair and the homeostasis recovery might be associated with the participation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs), both lung resident and migratory MSCs, these cells are characterized by their plasticity and immunomodulatory capacity, which are relevant to restoring tissue homeostasis after injury. However, RSV and HMPV may also infect MSCs, raising the question that infected MSCs could lose immunomodulatory efficacy and plasticity, thereby affecting tissue renewal. This review aims to provide an overview of the effect of respiratory viral infections, their implications in the lung tissue damage and the possible participation of MSCs in the recovery of lung homeostasis by tissue repair and immune response modulation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

papers.title_zh: MSC-RSV/HMPV 界面:对肺稳态、重塑以及非特应性哮喘和 COPD 风险的影响
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory tract infections continue to represent a major cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality. Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) are highlighted as key etiologic agents of bronchiolitis and pneumonia, particularly in children under two years old. Recurrent infections during the second year of life may be associated with significant histopathological damage and might also be a risk factor for developing chronic pulmonary diseases, such as non-atopic asthma. In adults, these viruses similarly elevate clinical burden on the elderly and individuals with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), causing the exacerbation of respiratory signals and symptoms and, consequently, promoting a chronic inflammatory response that modifies the lung tissue and disease progression. Tissue repair and the homeostasis recovery might be associated with the participation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs), both lung resident and migratory MSCs, these cells are characterized by their plasticity and immunomodulatory capacity, which are relevant to restoring tissue homeostasis after injury. However, RSV and HMPV may also infect MSCs, raising the question that infected MSCs could lose immunomodulatory efficacy and plasticity, thereby affecting tissue renewal. This review aims to provide an overview of the effect of respiratory viral infections, their implications in the lung tissue damage and the possible participation of MSCs in the recovery of lung homeostasis by tissue repair and immune response modulation.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染仍然是儿科发病和 死亡率 的主要原因。呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 被认为是 毛细支气管炎 和肺炎的关键病原体,特别是在两岁以下的儿童中。生命第二年的反复感染可能与显着的组织病理学损伤有关,也可能是发展为慢性肺部疾病(例如非特应性哮喘)的危险因素。在成人中,这些病毒同样会加重老年人和慢性阻塞性肺疾病(COPD)患者的临床负担,导致呼吸信号和症状加剧,从而促进慢性炎症反应,从而改变肺组织和疾病进展。组织修复和稳态恢复可能与间充质干细胞(MSC)的参与有关,包括肺常驻和迁移的MSC,这些细胞的特点是可塑性和免疫调节能力,与损伤后恢复组织稳态有关。然而,RSV和HMPV也可能感染MSC,这就提出了一个问题:受感染的MSC可能会失去免疫调节功效和可塑性,从而影响组织更新。本综述旨在概述呼吸道病毒感染的影响、其对肺组织损伤的影响以及间充质干细胞通过组织修复和 免疫应答 调节恢复肺稳态的可能参与。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.title: Diagnostic performance of antigen-based rapid test kits for six respiratory viruses in children: comparison with a multiplex PCR panel and correlation with viral load.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid antigen tests are widely used for point-of-care diagnosis of respiratory tract infection (RTI) in children, but how the sensitivity is influenced by viral load has not been comprehensively characterized across multiple pediatric respiratory viruses. In this prospective, paired-specimen study conducted at the pediatric center, two simultaneous nasopharyngeal swabs were obtained from children with RTI. One swab was tested using antigen-based rapid test kits (ImunoAce series, Tauns Laboratories, Inc.) for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and respiratory syncytial virus; the other was tested using the FilmArray Respiratory Panel (bioMérieux). Specimens positive by either method underwent confirmatory quantitative real-time PCR to determine viral load. Sensitivity was stratified by viral load. A total of 1,584 paired specimens from 1,232 children (median age: 3.0 years [IQR: 1.0–6.0]; 53.7% male) were analyzed. Sensitivity of the antigen tests ranged from 20.6% (adenovirus) to 79.7% (hMPV), while specificity exceeded 99% for all six targets and overall agreement ranged from 90.7% to 99.0%. For every virus, antigen test positivity increased steeply with viral load, approaching 90–100% at viral loads ≥10 6 –10 7 copies/100 μL and falling below 50% at loads ≤10 4 –10 5 copies/100 μL. Antigen-based rapid tests for common pediatric respiratory viruses showed high specificity and viral-load-dependent sensitivity, detecting nearly all specimens with high viral load regardless of the target virus. These findings support a role for antigen testing in identifying children with the highest viral burden—who are most likely to have acute infection. IMPORTANCE The sensitivity of rapid antigen tests for respiratory viruses relative to PCR-based testing has been incompletely characterized. This study evaluated antigen tests for six common pediatric respiratory viruses—SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and respiratory syncytial virus—against a multiplex PCR reference standard across 1,584 clinical specimens and linked test performance directly to quantitative viral load. We show that antigen test sensitivity is strongly and consistently dependent on viral load, approaching 90–100% at high viral loads with very high specificity across all six targets. These findings clarify the clinical role of rapid antigen testing: it reliably identifies children with the highest viral burden, who are most likely to have acute, symptomatic infection warranting immediate clinical action.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估基于抗原的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 快速检测的敏感性如何受到病毒载量的影响,因为儿童呼吸道病毒的这种关系尚未得到充分表征。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性配对样本研究是在儿科中心进行的,从 1,232 名患有呼吸道感染的儿童(中位年龄:3.0 岁 [IQR:1.0–6.0];53.7% 男性)同时采集了两份鼻咽拭子。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基于抗原的快速检测试剂盒(ImunoAce 系列,Tauns Laboratories,Inc.)对一根拭子进行 RSV 和其他呼吸道病毒的检测,而另一根拭子则使用 FilmArray 呼吸面板(bioMérieux)进行检测。任一方法呈阳性的样本均需进行验证性定量实时 PCR 以确定病毒载量。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV 抗原检测的敏感性范围为 20.6%(腺病毒)至 79.7%(hMPV),而所有六个目标的特异性均超过 99%。对于 RSV,抗原检测阳性率随病毒载量急剧增加,病毒载量≥10^6–10^7 拷贝/100 μL 时接近 90–100%,病毒载量≤10^4–10^5 拷贝/100 μL 时下降到 50% 以下。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,RSV 抗原测试的敏感性强烈且一致地依赖于病毒载量,并且对所有目标具有非常高的特异性。这凸显了抗原检测在识别病毒负荷最高的儿童方面的效用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果阐明了 RSV 快速抗原检测的临床作用,显示了其在检测高病毒载量病例方面的可靠性,这些病例最有可能代表需要立即采取临床行动的急性症状感染。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于来自单个儿科中心的配对标本,这可能会影响普遍性。然而,证据是强有力的,RSV 具有高特异性和明显的病毒载量依赖性敏感性。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from a Tertiary-Care Pediatric Cohort
papers.abstract: Objective: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infection in children. This study aimed to describe the clinical and laboratory characteristics of RSV-positive children older than 28 days in a tertiary-care cohort, explore characteristics associated with hospitalization in group comparisons, and identify factors independently associated with pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission among hospitalized children.Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study screened RSV testing records between August 2020 and August 2022 and included children older than 28 days with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection identified between February 2021 and August 2022. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, hospitalization, PICU admission, respiratory support, and outcome data were recorded. Comparisons were performed according to hospitalization status, clinical diagnosis, and PICU admission. A prespecified parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model evaluated factors associated with PICU admission among hospitalized children.Results: Of the 3523 children with available RSV test results during the study period, 561 RSV-positive children aged >28 days were included. Median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-14), and 317 patients (56.5%) were male. Bronchiolitis was the most common diagnosis (63.5%), followed by pneumonia (28.5%) and upper respiratory tract infection (8.0%). Hospitalization was required in 478 patients (85.2%), and 35 (6.2%) required PICU admission. Pneumonia was associated with higher rates of hypoxia, noninvasive ventilatory support, PICU admission, longer hospitalization, and delayed clinical improvement. Documented viral coinfection was detected in 30 patients (5.3%); no association was detected between documented viral coinfections and hospitalizations or PICU admission in this dataset. In hospitalized patients, pneumonia (OR, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.07-6.24; p=0.034) and hypoxia (OR, 32.08; 95% CI, 13.09-78.66; p<0.001) were independently associated with PICU admission.Conclusion: RSV infection predominantly affected infants and most commonly presented as bronchiolitis. Pneumonia and hypoxia were independently associated with PICU admission in this tertiary-care cohort.

Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, hospitalization, PICU admission, respiratory support, and outcome data were recorded. Comparisons were performed according to hospitalization status, clinical diagnosis, and PICU admission. A prespecified parsimonious multivariable logistic regression model evaluated factors associated with PICU admission among hospitalized children.Results: Of the 3523 children with available RSV test results during the study period, 561 RSV-positive children aged >28 days were included. Median age was 4 months (IQR, 2-14), and 317 patients (56.5%) were male. Bronchiolitis was the most common diagnosis (63.5%), followed by pneumonia (28.5%) and upper respiratory tract infection (8.0%). Pneumonia was associated with higher rates of hypoxia, noninvasive ventilatory support, PICU admission, longer hospitalization, and delayed clinical improvement. Documented viral coinfection was detected in 30 patients (5.3%); no association was detected between documented viral coinfections and hospitalizations or PICU admission in this dataset. Pneumonia and hypoxia were independently associated with PICU admission in this tertiary-care cohort.

papers.title: Bardoxolone methyl exerts an inhibitory effect on respiratory syncytial virus infection by downregulating IL-6 via the IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, but therapeutic options for active infection remain limited. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) contributes to RSV replication and RSV-induced inflammation, and the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway is a major regulator of IL-6 expression. Bardoxolone methyl (BXM) was identified by network medicine as a potential anti-RSV compound, with molecular docking suggesting interactions with the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway. We investigated whether BXM inhibits RSV infection through modulation of the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis in RSV-infected BEAS-2B cells and BALB/c mice. RSV infection increased IL-6 expression and activated IKKβ/NF-κB signaling, whereas IL-6 knockdown reduced viral replication and inflammatory mediator expression. BXM significantly suppressed RSV replication, as shown by RT-qPCR, TCID50, plaque reduction assays, and Western blotting, and decreased IL-6 expression in vitro . Mechanistically, BXM attenuated RSV-induced phosphorylation of IKKβ and NF-κB. The IKKβ inhibitor TPCA-1 produced similar inhibitory effects, whereas recombinant human IL-6 add-back partially restored inflammatory mediator expression in BXM-treated RSV-infected cells. In mice, BXM reduced lung viral titers, RSV-F expression, IL-6 expression, IKKβ/NF-κB activation, and RSV-induced lung injury. These findings suggest that BXM suppresses RSV replication and inflammation, at least in part, by modulating the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for RSV infection. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness, especially in infants, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. Although preventive strategies are available for some high-risk groups, treatment options for active RSV infection remain limited. This study identifies bardoxolone methyl (BXM) as a potential anti-RSV compound and shows that it can reduce both viral replication and virus-induced inflammation in cell and mouse models. Importantly, our findings suggest that BXM acts, at least in part, by reducing IL-6-related inflammatory signaling, which is closely associated with RSV disease severity. These results provide experimental evidence supporting BXM as a promising candidate for further development against RSV infection and offer insight into a potential host-targeted therapeutic strategy.

papers.title_zh: Bardoxolonemethyl 通过 IKKβ/NF-κB 信号通路下调 IL-6 对 呼吸道合胞病毒 感染产生抑制作用
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, but therapeutic options for active infection remain limited. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) contributes to RSV replication and RSV-induced inflammation, and the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway is a major regulator of IL-6 expression. Bardoxolone methyl (BXM) was identified by network medicine as a potential anti-RSV compound, with molecular docking suggesting interactions with the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway. We investigated whether BXM inhibits RSV infection through modulation of the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis in RSV-infected BEAS-2B cells and BALB/c mice. RSV infection increased IL-6 expression and activated IKKβ/NF-κB signaling, whereas IL-6 knockdown reduced viral replication and inflammatory mediator expression. BXM significantly suppressed RSV replication, as shown by RT-qPCR, TCID50, plaque reduction assays, and Western blotting, and decreased IL-6 expression in vitro . Mechanistically, BXM attenuated RSV-induced phosphorylation of IKKβ and NF-κB. The IKKβ inhibitor TPCA-1 produced similar inhibitory effects, whereas recombinant human IL-6 add-back partially restored inflammatory mediator expression in BXM-treated RSV-infected cells. In mice, BXM reduced lung viral titers, RSV-F expression, IL-6 expression, IKKβ/NF-κB activation, and RSV-induced lung injury. These findings suggest that BXM suppresses RSV replication and inflammation, at least in part, by modulating the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for RSV infection. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness, especially in infants, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. Although preventive strategies are available for some high-risk groups, treatment options for active RSV infection remain limited. This study identifies bardoxolone methyl (BXM) as a potential anti-RSV compound and shows that it can reduce both viral replication and virus-induced inflammation in cell and mouse models. Importantly, our findings suggest that BXM acts, at least in part, by reducing IL-6-related inflammatory signaling, which is closely associated with RSV disease severity. These results provide experimental evidence supporting BXM as a promising candidate for further development against RSV infection and offer insight into a potential host-targeted therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Coinfections With Respiratory Syncytial Virus in a Cohort of Adults With High‐Risk Conditions, 2015–2020: A Retrospective Observational Study
papers.abstract: Summary Coinfections may influence the clinical outcome of respiratory illness. Data are limited regarding RSV coinfections in adults with high‐risk conditions. Residual respiratory specimens from community‐dwelling adults (≥ 18 years) with ≥ 1 high‐risk condition were retested using a multiplex panel for multiple viral pathogens. We compared demographic and clinical characteristics between those with RSV coinfection versus RSV single infection. RSV coinfections comprised 5.9% of all RSV infections among adults with ≥ 1 high‐risk condition. No statistically significant differences were observed between those with RSV coinfections and single infections according to presence of specific high‐risk conditions or clinical disease presentation.
