analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the impact of RSV coinfections on clinical outcomes in adults with high-risk conditions. The background highlights that coinfections may influence the clinical outcome of respiratory illness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective observational study was conducted using residual respiratory specimens from community-dwelling adults (≥ 18 years) with ≥ 1 high-risk condition. The study spanned from 2015 to 2020.
analysis.methods: Residual respiratory specimens were retested using a multiplex panel to detect multiple viral pathogens. The study compared demographic and clinical characteristics between individuals with RSV coinfection and those with RSV single infection.
analysis.main_results: RSV coinfections accounted for 5.9% of all RSV infections among adults with ≥ 1 high-risk condition. No statistically significant differences were observed between those with RSV coinfections and single infections regarding specific high-risk conditions or clinical disease presentation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that RSV coinfections are relatively common in adults with high-risk conditions but do not appear to significantly affect clinical outcomes compared to single infections. This study provides a descriptive analysis of RSV coinfections in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to understanding the epidemiology of RSV coinfections in adults with high-risk conditions, which may inform future surveillance and diagnostic strategies for respiratory illnesses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on residual specimens, which may introduce selection bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study examined RSV coinfections in adults with high-risk conditions from 2015 to 2020. The research aimed to understand how coinfections might influence clinical outcomes in respiratory illness. Using a multiplex panel, residual respiratory specimens were retested to identify multiple viral pathogens. The study found that RSV coinfections made up 5.9% of all RSV infections in this population. However, no significant differences were observed between those with coinfections and single infections in terms of specific high-risk conditions or clinical disease presentation. The findings suggest that RSV coinfections are common but do not significantly alter clinical outcomes. This study provides descriptive insights into RSV coinfections, which may help improve surveillance and diagnostic approaches. The evidence is moderate due to the retrospective design and potential selection bias.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 RSV 合并感染对高危成人临床结果的影响。背景强调,合并感染可能会影响呼吸道疾病的临床结果。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用患有 ≥ 1 种高危病症的社区居住成年人(≥ 18 岁)的残留呼吸道标本进行了一项回顾性观察研究。该研究的时间跨度为2015年至2020年。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多重检测板重新测试残留的呼吸道样本,以检测多种病毒病原体。该研究比较了 RSV 合并感染者和 RSV 单一感染者之间的人口统计和临床特征。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,RSV 合并感染在患有高危疾病的成年人中相对常见,但与单一感染相比,似乎不会显着影响临床结果。本研究对该人群中 RSV 合并感染进行了描述性分析。

analysis_en.methods: Residual respiratory specimens were retested using a multiplex panel to detect multiple viral pathogens. The study compared demographic and clinical characteristics between individuals with RSV coinfection and those with RSV single infection.
analysis_en.main_results: RSV coinfections accounted for 5.9% of all RSV infections among adults with ≥ 1 high-risk condition. analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on residual specimens, which may introduce selection bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

papers.title: Đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của vi rút hợp bào hô hấp trên bệnh nhân nhi viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng (SARI) tại miền Bắc Việt Nam, 2017-2020 Molecular Evolution of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Pediatric Patients with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) in Northern Viet Nam, 2017-2020
papers.abstract: Vi rút hợp bào hô hấp ở người (Respiratory Syncytial Virus – RSV) là một trong những nguyên nhân hàng đầu gây nhiễm trùng đường hô hấp cấp tính ở trẻ nhỏ. Các nghiên cứu về đặc điểm sinh học phân tử và tiến hoá của RSV vẫn còn hạn chế tại những quốc gia có thu nhập thấp và trung bình. Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm xác định đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của RSV trên bệnh nhân nhi nhiễm trùng hô hấp cấp tính nặng tại miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2017–2020. Từ các mẫu viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng được xác định dương tính với RSV tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương và Bệnh viện đa khoa tỉnh Quảng Ninh trong 4 năm (2017-2020) tiến hành lựa chọn 56 mẫu dương tính RSV-A và 50 mẫu dương tính RSV-B để giải trình tự toàn bộ gen G bằng kỹ thuật giải trình tự gen thế hệ mới. Các mẫu này được lựa chọn theo giá trị Ct, phân nhóm, tuổi, giới tính, thời gian lấy mẫu và địa điểm. Từ kết quả giải trình tự, các phân tích phát sinh chủng loại và tiến hóa được thực hiện để phân tích đặc điểm tiến hoá phân tử. Kết quả cho thấy các chủng RSV-A đều thuộc clade A.D, kiểu gen ON1 (53 chủng) và non-ON1 (3 chủng), 50 chủng RSV-B thuộc clade B.D.4, kiểu gen BA9. Tất cả các chủng RSV-A của Việt Nam trong nghiên cứ này đều không có đoạn lặp 72 nucleotide ở vùng siêu biến đổi thứ hai trên gen G. Tốc độ tiến hóa phân tử ước tính của gen G RSV-A và RSV-B lần lượt là 1,32 × 10-3 và 8,29 × 10-4 thay thế/ vị trí/năm. Các vị trí N-glycosyl hóa và các vị trí axit amin chịu áp lực chọn lọc ở cả hai phân nhóm vi rút cũng được xác định. Nghiên cứu đã đưa ra được tốc độ tiến hóa và các đặc điểm tiến hoá phân tử của cả RSV-A và RSV-B tại miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2017-2020, góp phần cung cấp các dữ liệu cho việc thực hiện giám sát sự lưu hành của vi rút này trong thời gian tới tại Việt Nam.
papers.journal: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng

papers.title_original: Đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của vi rút hợp bào hô hấp trên bệnh nhân nhi viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng (SARI) tại miền Bắc Việt Nam, 2017-2020 Molecular Evolution of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Pediatric Patients with Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) in Northern Viet Nam, 2017-2020

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the molecular evolutionary characteristics of human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in pediatric patients with severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020, addressing the limited research on RSV molecular evolution in low- and middle-income countries.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted on RSV-positive samples from pediatric patients with SARI at two hospitals in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020, focusing on 56 RSV-A and 50 RSV-B samples.
analysis.methods: The study involved selecting RSV-positive samples based on Ct values, grouping, age, gender, sampling time, and location, then sequencing the entire G gene using next-generation sequencing technology.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that all RSV-A strains belonged to clade A.D, with 53 ON1 and 3 non-ON1 genotypes, while all RSV-B strains belonged to clade B.D.4, with the BA9 genotype. The molecular evolution rates of the G gene for RSV-A and RSV-B were estimated to be 1.32 × 10-3 and 8.29 × 10-4 substitutions per site per year, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provided the molecular evolutionary characteristics of both RSV-A and RSV-B in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020, contributing to the surveillance of RSV circulation in the region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the surveillance and monitoring of RSV circulation in northern Vietnam, aiding in the prevention and control of RSV infections in pediatric patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the selection of samples based on specific criteria and the potential for sampling bias, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the molecular evolutionary characteristics of RSV in pediatric patients with SARI in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020. The study involved sequencing the G gene of 56 RSV-A and 50 RSV-B samples, showing that all RSV-A strains belonged to clade A.D and all RSV-B strains belonged to clade B.D.4. The study provided the molecular evolutionary characteristics of both RSV-A and RSV-B, contributing to the surveillance and monitoring of RSV circulation in the region.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在确定2017年至2020年越南北部严重急性呼吸道感染(SARI)儿科患者中人类呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的分子进化特征,解决低收入和中等收入国家对RSV分子进化的有限研究。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对 2017 年至 2020 年越南北部两家医院的 SARI 儿科患者的 RSV 阳性样本进行,重点关注 56 个 RSV-A 和 50 个 RSV-B 样本。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究包括根据Ct值、分组、年龄、性别、采样时间和地点选择RSV阳性样本,然后使用下一代测序技术对整个G基因进行测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,所有RSV-A株均属于A.D进化枝,有53个ON1和3个非ON1基因型;所有RSV-B株均属于B.D.4进化枝,有BA9基因型。RSV-A 和 RSV-B 的 G 基因的分子 进化 率估计分别为每年每个位点 1.32 × 10-3 和 8.29 × 10-4 替换。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了2017年至2020年越南北部RSV-A和RSV-B的分子进化特征,有助于该地区RSV循环的监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为 监测 和越南北部 RSV 循环监测提供信息,有助于预防和控制儿科患者的 RSV 感染。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括根据特定标准选择样本以及潜在的抽样偏差,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the molecular evolutionary characteristics of human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in pediatric patients with severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020, addressing the limited research on RSV molecular evolution in low- and middle-income countries.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted on RSV-positive samples from pediatric patients with SARI at two hospitals in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020, focusing on 56 RSV-A and 50 RSV-B samples.
analysis_en.methods: The study involved selecting RSV-positive samples based on Ct values, grouping, age, gender, sampling time, and location, then sequencing the entire G gene using next-generation sequencing technology.
analysis_en.main_results: The results showed that all RSV-A strains belonged to clade A.D, with 53 ON1 and 3 non-ON1 genotypes, while all RSV-B strains belonged to clade B.D.4, with the BA9 genotype. The molecular evolution rates of the G gene for RSV-A and RSV-B were estimated to be 1.32 × 10-3 and 8.29 × 10-4 substitutions per site per year, respectively.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provided the molecular evolutionary characteristics of both RSV-A and RSV-B in northern Vietnam from 2017 to 2020, contributing to the surveillance of RSV circulation in the region.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the surveillance and monitoring of RSV circulation in northern Vietnam, aiding in the prevention and control of RSV infections in pediatric patients.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the selection of samples based on specific criteria and the potential for sampling bias, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

papers.title_zh: Đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của vi rút hợp bào hô hấp trên bệnh nhân nhi viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng (SARI) tại miền Bắc 越南,2017-2020 越南北部严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 儿科患者中人 呼吸道合胞病毒 的分子 进化,2017-2020
papers.source_body_en: Vi rút hợp bào hô hấp ở người (Respiratory Syncytial Virus – RSV) là một trong những nguyên nhân hàng đầu gây nhiễm trùng đường hô hấp cấp tính ở trẻ nhỏ. Các nghiên cứu về đặc điểm sinh học phân tử và tiến hoá của RSV vẫn còn hạn chế tại những quốc gia có thu nhập thấp và trung bình. Nghiên cứu này được thực hiện nhằm xác định đặc điểm tiến hóa phân tử của RSV trên bệnh nhân nhi nhiễm trùng hô hấp cấp tính nặng tại miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2017–2020. Từ các mẫu viêm đường hô hấp cấp tính nặng được xác định dương tính với RSV tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương và Bệnh viện đa khoa tỉnh Quảng Ninh trong 4 năm (2017-2020) tiến hành lựa chọn 56 mẫu dương tính RSV-A và 50 mẫu dương tính RSV-B để giải trình tự toàn bộ gen G bằng kỹ thuật giải trình tự gen thế hệ mới. Các mẫu này được lựa chọn theo giá trị Ct, phân nhóm, tuổi, giới tính, thời gian lấy mẫu và địa điểm. Từ kết quả giải trình tự, các phân tích phát sinh chủng loại và tiến hóa được thực hiện để phân tích đặc điểm tiến hoá phân tử. Kết quả cho thấy các chủng RSV-A đều thuộc clade A.D, kiểu gen ON1 (53 chủng) và non-ON1 (3 chủng), 50 chủng RSV-B thuộc clade B.D.4, kiểu gen BA9. Tất cả các chủng RSV-A của Việt Nam trong nghiên cứ này đều không có đoạn lặp 72 nucleotide ở vùng siêu biến đổi thứ hai trên gen G. Tốc độ tiến hóa phân tử ước tính của gen G RSV-A và RSV-B lần lượt là 1,32 × 10-3 và 8,29 × 10-4 thay thế/ vị trí/năm. Các vị trí N-glycosyl hóa và các vị trí axit amin chịu áp lực chọn lọc ở cả hai phân nhóm vi rút cũng được xác định. Nghiên cứu đã đưa ra được tốc độ tiến hóa và các đặc điểm tiến hoá phân tử của cả RSV-A và RSV-B tại miền Bắc Việt Nam giai đoạn 2017-2020, góp phần cung cấp các dữ liệu cho việc thực hiện giám sát sự lưu hành của vi rút này trong thời gian tới tại Việt Nam.

papers.title: Classifying and Differentiating Clinical Coding of Respiratory Syncytial Virus, Influenza, and COVID-19 in OpenSAFELY Between 2016 and 2024
papers.abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) are a rich source of data which can be used to analyse health outcomes using computable phenotypes. With the approval of NHS England we used the OpenSAFELY secure analytics platform to design and assess phenotypes to classify three key respiratory viruses - respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and COVID-19 - in English coded health data between September 2016 and August 2024. We compared narrow and broad phenotypes to one another and to publicly available surveillance data. Cases from both phenotypes showed similar seasonal patterns to surveillance data. Broad phenotypes led to increased risk of misclassification than narrow phenotypes for mild cases. For severe cases the risk of misclassification was higher in infants than for older adults, irrespective of the phenotype used. The phenotypes presented here offer a potential route to classify respiratory viruses from coded health records in the absence of testing information.

papers.title: RSV Bivalent Prefusion F Protein Vaccine in Pregnancy and Protection Against RSV-Associated Illness in Infants: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy has demonstrated efficacy in protecting infants against early-life RSV disease in the pivotal clinical trial. OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize real-world evidence on the effectiveness of RSVpreF in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC were searched from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. STUDY SELECTION: A total of 1144 studies were initially identified. Eligible were nonrandomized studies reporting the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in pregnancy in the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI in infants. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: All studies were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data were extracted on RSV-associated outcomes among infants born to women who received RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and infants born to unvaccinated women. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization. Odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was calculated as (1 - OR) × 100% and assessed in infants from birth to age 3 months and from birth to 6 months, separately. The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against the secondary outcomes of RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. RESULTS: A total of 7 studies were included, comprising 7112 infants, of whom 2684 were born to vaccinated mothers. The studies collected data from January 2024 through April 2025 from Argentina, the UK, and the US. Pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%; 3 studies, 4397 participants; I2 = 0%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%; 6 studies, 3008 participants; I2 = 18.7%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that postimplementation data support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life. The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs.

papers.title: [Update on vaccination for older adults].
papers.abstract: Older adults are highly susceptible to infections, some of which are vaccine preventable. Therefore, the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) regularly updates its vaccination recommendations for older adults as well. Since the 2025/26 season, the adjuvanted influenza vaccine is recommended for people aged 60 and older, in addition to the high-dose influenza vaccine. In addition, a one-time vaccination against respiratory syncytial virus in autumn has been added as a routine vaccination for 75-year-olds and as an indication-based vaccination for those aged 60 and older with severe underlying medical conditions. Little attention has been paid so far to the now well documented additional benefits of vaccinations against shingles, pneumococcal disease, influenza, and RSV - that is, effects that go beyond the primary therapeutic benefit and make a significant contribution to healthy aging. These include a reduction in myocardial and cerebrovascular events, as well as a protective effect against neurodegenerative processes. In particular it has been demonstrated that the influenza vaccine is as effective as statins in the secondary prevention of myocardial infarction. These findings could lead to an increased acceptance of vaccination and, consequently, to an increase in vaccination rates, which remain insufficient. To continue improving the benefits of vaccination in the future, vaccines need to be further developed to achieve greater efficacy, which could also help increase acceptance of vaccination. Several new developments are currently in the pipeline, particularly for the pneumococcal vaccine. Since March 2025, a 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for adults has been licensed in Europe, specifically targeting the serotypes that cause IPD in adults. Additional pneumococcal vaccine candidates covering up to 31 serotypes are currently in development using new technologies and are undergoing Phase 2 or 3 trials.

source_records.title: Update Impfungen im Alter
source_records.abstract: Für die Influenzaimpfung werden nun alternativ 2 Vakzine empfohlen, zum einen der bereits zuvor schon empfohlene Hochdosisgrippeimpfstoff, zum anderen neu ein adjuvantierter Grippeimpfstoff. Neu hinzugekommen ist die einmalige Impfung im Herbst gegen RSV als Standardimpfung für die ab 75-Jährigen sowie als Indikationsimpfung für ab 60-Jährige mit schweren Vorerkrankungen. Es entfällt die Empfehlung zum Erlangen der Basisimmunität für die erwachsene Bevölkerung. Die Altersgrenze für die jährliche Standard-COVID-19-Auffrischimpfung wird von 60 auf 75 Jahre angehoben. Für einen bestmöglichen Impfschutz sollte die jährliche COVID-19-Auffrischimpfung zu Beginn der COVID-19-Saison im Spätsommer/Frühherbst erfolgen. Mittlerweile ist gut belegt, dass die Vakzinierung gegen Herpes zoster, Pneumokokken, Influenza und RSV signifikante „Off-Target-Effekte“, also Wirkungen, die über den primär therapeutischen Effekt hinausgehen, besitzt. Zu diesen gehören die Reduktion myokardialer und zerebrovaskulärer Ereignisse sowie eine protektive Wirkung gegen neurodegenerative Prozesse. Insbesondere für die Influenzaimpfung ist belegt, dass sie in der Sekundärprävention des Myokardinfarktes eine vergleichbare Wirksamkeit hat wie Statine. In Europa ist seit 03/2025 ein 21-valenter Pneumokokkenkonjugatimpfstoff für Erwachsene zugelassen. source_records.abstract: Für die Influenzaimpfung werden nun alternativ 2 Vakzine empfohlen, zum einen der bereits zuvor schon empfohlene Hochdosisgrippeimpfstoff, zum anderen neu ein adjuvantierter Grippeimpfstoff. Neu hinzugekommen ist die einmalige Impfung im Herbst gegen RSV als Standardimpfung für die ab 75-Jährigen sowie als Indikationsimpfung für ab 60-Jährige mit schweren Vorerkrankungen. It emphasizes that the Standing Committee on Vaccination (STIKO) regularly updates its recommendations for this population. The adjuvanted influenza vaccine and high-dose influenza vaccine are recommended for individuals aged 60 and older since the 2025/26 season. Additionally, a one-time RSV vaccination is introduced for 75-year-olds and for those aged 60 and older with severe underlying medical conditions. The review also notes that the influenza vaccine has been shown to be as effective as statins in the secondary prevention of myocardial infarction. papers.title: RSV Disease Among Hospitalized Children: Second vs. First Year of Life Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric hospitalization, yet data on children hospitalized with RSV in their second year of life are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics and management practices of children hospitalized with RSV during their second versus first year of life. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included children aged 0-23 months hospitalized with RSV infection across 11 medical centers between 2017 and 2021. We compared demographics, outcomes (length of stay [LOS] > 3 days, and pediatric intensive care unit [PICU] admission), and systemic corticosteroid and antibiotic use between the second and first years of life, adjusting for prematurity, comorbidities, and the COVID-19 pandemic. RESULTS: Among 6260 children hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, 1321 (21%) were hospitalized during their second year of life. Compared with first-year admissions, second-year patients had higher rates of prematurity (18.0% vs. 13.4%) and comorbidities (6.3% vs. 2.6%) (both p < 0.001). They more frequently received corticosteroids (53.5% vs. 23.2%) and antibiotics (63.4% vs. 45.9%) (both p < 0.001) and had lower PICU admission rates (4.6% vs. 7.0%; p < 0 0.001) and similar rates of prolonged LOS (35.0% vs. In adjusted analyses, second-year hospitalization was associated with increased corticosteroid use (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.28; 95% CI, 3.67-4.99) and antibiotic use (aOR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.80-2.43), and lower odds of PICU admission (aOR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.40-0.79). CONCLUSIONS: RSV hospitalization in the second year of life carries a significant burden, with higher antibiotic and corticosteroid use despite lower PICU rates and similar LOS. These findings highlight the need for better characterization of this age group to optimize future immunoprophylaxis strategies.

papers.title: RSV Disease Burden in Adults in Emerging Market Countries, a Systematic Review and Modelling Analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Most previous studies on adult respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) burden focus on high-income settings (HIC). With the recent approval of RSV vaccines for adults, extending epidemiological understanding to emerging market countries (EMC) is critical for informing prevention strategies. We aimed to characterize the burden of RSV among adults ≥18 years in EMC. Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSEPRO: CRD420251137828) to identify studies reporting estimates of RSV burden from any care setting in adults>18 years in EMC. For each individual study included, we followed a two-step statistical approach to adjust for RSV case under-ascertainment related to the use of clinical specimen and diagnostic test. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate RSV incidence rate, proportion positive, hospitalisation, and mortality burden. Findings We included 70 studies of which the majority were from China (30/70) and PCR was the predominant diagnostic method (59/70). Adjusted RSV disease incidence rate (approximately 2.5 times higher than unadjusted) ranged from 2,544 (95% CI 1,352-4,787) per 100,000 in adults aged 18-49 years to 2,392 (1,618-3,534) in adults ≥65 years after accounting for clinical sampling and diagnostic testing. Adjusted hospitalisation rates increased with age, from 20 (8-51) per 100,000 in 18-49 years to 74 (3-2,027) in adults ≥65 years, representing an approximate 2.5-fold increase after adjustment. The adjusted RSV proportion positive was relatively stable, ranging from 1.8% (0.4-8.5) to 9.7% (6.3-14.6), regardless of settings or clinical case definitions. The unadjusted in-hospital case fatality ratio (hCFR) was 6.0% (2.9-11.9) in adults ≥65 years vs 3.1 (2.0-5.0) in those 18-49 years. Among hospitalized RSV-positive adults, 95.8% (84.2-99.0) had at least one comorbidity, most commonly hypertension, diabetes, and COPD. Conclusion The estimated incidence and proportion positive of RSV disease in EMC is substantially lower than HIC. Narrow case definitions requiring fever, less sensitive testing such as direct fluorescent antibody testing, reduced healthcare access, and incomplete surveillance may be contributing to these lower estimates. In-hospital CFR are comparable to or higher than in HIC.

We aimed to characterize the burden of RSV among adults ≥18 years in EMC. Methods We conducted a systematic review (PROSEPRO: CRD420251137828) to identify studies reporting estimates of RSV burden from any care setting in adults>18 years in EMC. For each individual study included, we followed a two-step statistical approach to adjust for RSV case under-ascertainment related to the use of clinical specimen and diagnostic test. Random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to estimate RSV incidence rate, proportion positive, hospitalisation, and mortality burden. Findings We included 70 studies of which the majority were from China (30/70) and PCR was the predominant diagnostic method (59/70). Adjusted RSV disease incidence rate (approximately 2.5 times higher than unadjusted) ranged from 2,544 (95% CI 1,352-4,787) per 100,000 in adults aged 18-49 years to 2,392 (1,618-3,534) in adults ≥65 years after accounting for clinical sampling and diagnostic testing. Adjusted hospitalisation rates increased with age, from 20 (8-51) per 100,000 in 18-49 years to 74 (3-2,027) in adults ≥65 years, representing an approximate 2.5-fold increase after adjustment. The adjusted RSV proportion positive was relatively stable, ranging from 1.8% (0.4-8.5) to 9.7% (6.3-14.6), regardless of settings or clinical case definitions. The unadjusted in-hospital case fatality ratio (hCFR) was 6.0% (2.9-11.9) in adults ≥65 years vs 3.1 (2.0-5.0) in those 18-49 years. Among hospitalized RSV-positive adults, 95.8% (84.2-99.0) had at least one comorbidity, most commonly hypertension, diabetes, and COPD. Conclusion The estimated incidence and proportion positive of RSV disease in EMC is substantially lower than HIC. Narrow case definitions requiring fever, less sensitive testing such as direct fluorescent antibody testing, reduced healthcare access, and incomplete surveillance may be contributing to these lower estimates. In-hospital CFR are comparable to or higher than in HIC.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and modelling analysis aimed to characterize the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults ≥18 years in emerging market countries (EMC). The review included 70 studies, predominantly from China, using PCR as the main diagnostic method. Adjusted RSV incidence rates were found to be 2,544 (95% CI 1,352-4,787) per 100,000 in adults aged 18-49 years and 2,392 (1,618-3,534) in adults ≥65 years. Adjusted hospitalisation rates increased with age, from 20 (8-51) per 100,000 in 18-49 years to 74 (3-2,027) in adults ≥65 years. The adjusted proportion positive of RSV was relatively stable, ranging from 1.8% (0.4-8.5) to 9.7% (6.3-14.6). The unadjusted in-hospital case fatality ratio (hCFR) was 6.0% (2.9-11.9) in adults ≥65 years versus 3.1% (2.0-5.0) in those aged 18-49 years. The study concluded that RSV disease burden in EMC is substantially lower than in high-income settings (HIC). The authors suggested that narrow case definitions, less sensitive testing, reduced healthcare access, and incomplete surveillance may contribute to these lower estimates. The findings highlight the importance of extending epidemiological understanding to EMC to inform RSV prevention strategies, especially with the recent approval of RSV vaccines for adults.

papers.title: Risk Factors for COVID-19 and Influenza Nonvaccination during the 2025-2026 Respiratory Season among a Cross-Sectional Sample of Older US Adults.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Adults aged ≥ 65 years are high-risk for severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and influenza outcomes, but reasons for nonvaccination remain understudied. METHODS: We estimated age- and gender-adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) among adults aged ≥ 65 years in the Communities, Households, and SARS-CoV-2 Epidemiology (CHASING) COVID Cohort living in the USA for two comparisons: (1) receiving neither the COVID-19 nor the influenza vaccine versus both vaccines, and (2) receiving only influenza versus both vaccines between September 2025 and March 2026. Reasons for nonreceipt are summarized. RESULTS: Among 649 participants, 42.1% did not receive the COVID-19 vaccine and 21.4% did not receive the influenza vaccine in the 2025-2026 respiratory season. Those with the lowest trust in their doctor (aPR: 5.56, 95% CI: 4.25-7.27), most difficulty asking their provider vaccine questions (aPR: 2.59, 95% CI: 1.70-3.94), lowest perceived community benefit of influenza (aPR: 12.25, 95% CI: 8.58-17.49) and COVID-19 (aPR: 12.12, 95% CI: 8.52-17.26) vaccination, and receipt of no other (respiratory syncytial virus [RSV], shingles, or pneumococcal) vaccine during the 2025-2026 respiratory season (aPR: 3.48, 95% CI: 2.13-5.66) had a higher likelihood of receiving neither versus both vaccines. These associations were attenuated when comparing receiving only influenza versus both the influenza and COVID-19 vaccines. Side effects and safety concerns were the most common reasons for not receiving the COVID-19 vaccine, though lack of a health care provider recommendation was a commonly reported reason among those who received ≥ 1 other vaccine (influenza, RSV, shingles, or pneumococcal) during the time period. For nonreceipt of the influenza vaccine, concerns about side effects and low perceived need were common reasons cited. CONCLUSIONS: Focused efforts are particularly needed to increase COVID-19 vaccination among this high-risk group. Health care providers should leverage clinical encounters to build trust, address safety and efficacy concerns, and ensure that older adults receive the full range of recommended vaccines, but reducing access barriers and building and maintaining trust in vaccines among older adults will likely also require a multipronged approach.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates risk factors for nonvaccination against COVID-19 and influenza among older US adults during the 2025-2026 respiratory season. It highlights that low trust in healthcare providers, difficulty in asking vaccine-related questions, and low perceived community benefit of vaccination are associated with not receiving both vaccines. The study found that 42.1% of participants did not receive the COVID-19 vaccine, while 21.4% did not receive the influenza vaccine. However, the evidence does not explicitly report limitations or the strength of the findings.

papers.title: Shifting viral aetiology, codetection and age-specific mortality in severe acute respiratory infection in Brazil, 2022-2025: a nationwide surveillance study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral aetiology and codetection among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications have evolved post-COVID-19. We examined temporal patterns, age heterogeneity, and severe outcome associations in Brazil. METHODS: We analysed nationwide SIVEP-Gripe SARI records (2022-2025; extracted July 2026) with RT-PCR viral detection. Seven mutually exclusive categories were evaluated using robust Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for SARI-attributed mortality and a severe composite outcome (ICU admission, invasive ventilation, or death). RESULTS: Among 447,107 virus-positive records, 7.2% involved codetections and 25.4% included RSV. Isolated SARS-CoV-2 declined from 72.4% (2022) to 6.8% (2025), while codetections rose from 3.0% to 11.2%. Compared to isolated RSV, mortality was higher for codetection without RSV (aRR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.67-1.94), isolated SARS-CoV-2 (1.62, 1.54-1.70), and codetection with RSV (1.40, 1.27-1.55). Associations varied by age ($p < .001$). Among RSV-positive cases, codetection conferred increased mortality risk (aRR 1.46, 1.32-1.61). Excluding isolated SARS-CoV-2 attenuated the 2025-versus-2022 codetection prevalence ratio from 1.85 to 1.10. CONCLUSIONS: Viral detections shifted towards greater heterogeneity, strongly driven by changing surveillance composition. Varying testing indications and panels limit causal inference. Integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting is essential; surveillance proportions do not reflect population incidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the evolving viral aetiology and codetection patterns in severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications in Brazil from 2022 to 2025. It highlights the shift in viral detection towards greater heterogeneity, driven by changes in surveillance composition. The findings reveal that codetection with RSV and other viruses is associated with increased mortality risk compared to isolated RSV cases. The study underscores the importance of integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting to accurately reflect population incidence. However, the study's limitations include the reliance on surveillance data, which may not capture true population trends due to varying testing indications and panels. The evidence suggests a moderate confidence level in the findings due to the observational nature of the study and potential biases in surveillance data.

papers.title_zh: 2022-2025 年巴西严重急性呼吸道感染的病毒病原学、联合检测和年龄特异性 死亡率 的变化:一项全国性 监测 研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral aetiology and codetection among severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) notifications have evolved post-COVID-19. We examined temporal patterns, age heterogeneity, and severe outcome associations in Brazil. METHODS: We analysed nationwide SIVEP-Gripe SARI records (2022-2025; extracted July 2026) with RT-PCR viral detection. Seven mutually exclusive categories were evaluated using robust Poisson regression to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for SARI-attributed mortality and a severe composite outcome (ICU admission, invasive ventilation, or death). RESULTS: Among 447,107 virus-positive records, 7.2% involved codetections and 25.4% included RSV. Isolated SARS-CoV-2 declined from 72.4% (2022) to 6.8% (2025), while codetections rose from 3.0% to 11.2%. Compared to isolated RSV, mortality was higher for codetection without RSV (aRR 1.80, 95% CI: 1.67-1.94), isolated SARS-CoV-2 (1.62, 1.54-1.70), and codetection with RSV (1.40, 1.27-1.55). Associations varied by age ($p < .001$). Among RSV-positive cases, codetection conferred increased mortality risk (aRR 1.46, 1.32-1.61). Excluding isolated SARS-CoV-2 attenuated the 2025-versus-2022 codetection prevalence ratio from 1.85 to 1.10. CONCLUSIONS: Viral detections shifted towards greater heterogeneity, strongly driven by changing surveillance composition. Varying testing indications and panels limit causal inference. Integrated, age-sensitive surveillance with standardized diagnostic reporting is essential; surveillance proportions do not reflect population incidence.

papers.title: Non-invasive quantification of lower airway antigen-specific antibodies using exhaled breath particles - an observational proof-of-concept study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Advancements in mucosal vaccine development highlight the urgent need for practical methods to assess immune responses in both upper and lower airways. Although nasal sampling is increasingly standardised, a non-invasive technique for directly assessing antigen-specific antibodies in the distal airways has been lacking. METHODS: We used Particles in Exhaled Air (PExA), a non-invasive method capturing aerosolised respiratory tract lining fluid (RTLF) from the distal airways, to quantify antigen-specific IgA and IgG. Antibodies were measured in paired serum, nasal secretions, and PExA samples from 28 healthcare workers during spring 2025, including 18 with RT-qPCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (H1N1), or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. FINDINGS: Antigen-specific IgA and IgG measurements in PExA samples showed low variability (median CVs: spike-IgA 3.7%, H1-IgA 7.2%, RSV pre-F-IgA 5.3%). Strong correlations (Spearman's rho >0.85, p < 0.0001) were observed between PExA and serum IgG, which may be consistent with a systemic contribution to lower-airway IgG levels. In contrast, IgA correlations were more modest, which may reflect local IgA production in the lungs. IgG and IgA correlated between PExA and nasal secretions, while the IgA/IgG ratio was higher in nasal secretions (median 5.0 vs 0.6, p < 0.0001), consistent with expected isotype distribution in upper and lower airways. INTERPRETATION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of non-invasive measurement of antigen-specific antibodies in the lower airways. Our approach proposes a framework for assessing lower-airway immunity and supporting next-generation mucosal vaccine development. FUNDING: This study was funded by the European Research Council, the Swedish Society for Medical Research, and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

analysis.summary_en: This observational proof-of-concept study explores the feasibility of non-invasive quantification of antigen-specific antibodies in the lower airways using exhaled breath particles (PExA). The research highlights the need for practical methods to assess immune responses in both upper and lower airways, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The study measured IgA and IgG in paired serum, nasal secretions, and PExA samples from 28 healthcare workers, including 18 with RT-qPCR-confirmed RSV infection. The findings demonstrate the potential of PExA as a tool for assessing lower-airway immunity and supporting mucosal vaccine development. However, the study's small sample size and observational nature limit its generalisability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 使用呼出气颗粒对下呼吸道抗原特异性抗体进行无创定量 - 一项观察性概念验证研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Advancements in mucosal vaccine development highlight the urgent need for practical methods to assess immune responses in both upper and lower airways. Although nasal sampling is increasingly standardised, a non-invasive technique for directly assessing antigen-specific antibodies in the distal airways has been lacking. METHODS: We used Particles in Exhaled Air (PExA), a non-invasive method capturing aerosolised respiratory tract lining fluid (RTLF) from the distal airways, to quantify antigen-specific IgA and IgG. Antibodies were measured in paired serum, nasal secretions, and PExA samples from 28 healthcare workers during spring 2025, including 18 with RT-qPCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (H1N1), or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. FINDINGS: Antigen-specific IgA and IgG measurements in PExA samples showed low variability (median CVs: spike-IgA 3.7%, H1-IgA 7.2%, RSV pre-F-IgA 5.3%). Strong correlations (Spearman's rho >0.85, p < 0.0001) were observed between PExA and serum IgG, which may be consistent with a systemic contribution to lower-airway IgG levels. In contrast, IgA correlations were more modest, which may reflect local IgA production in the lungs. IgG and IgA correlated between PExA and nasal secretions, while the IgA/IgG ratio was higher in nasal secretions (median 5.0 vs 0.6, p < 0.0001), consistent with expected isotype distribution in upper and lower airways. INTERPRETATION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of non-invasive measurement of antigen-specific antibodies in the lower airways. Our approach proposes a framework for assessing lower-airway immunity and supporting next-generation mucosal vaccine development. FUNDING: This study was funded by the European Research Council, the Swedish Society for Medical Research, and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

papers.title: Upper Airway and Neurological Manifestations of Pediatric Omicron Infection: From Novel Pathogen to Endemic Respiratory Virus — A Natural Experiment in Immuno-naive versus Primed Children
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The Omicron variant of SARS-CoV-2 has been associated with altered clinical phenotypes in children, including upper airway involvement and neurological complications. However, the magnitude of these manifestations relative to established pediatric respiratory viruses remains incompletely quantified, and the extent to which immune priming attenuates severity is unknown. We aimed to characterize upper airway obstruction (UAO) and neurological events in hospitalized children with Omicron infection, to compare outcomes with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human rhinovirus (HRV) using propensity score-matched analyzes, and to leverage a unique natural experiment to assess the impact of first versus second immune exposure on disease severity. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we identified 2,085 hospitalized children (0–18 years) with laboratory-confirmed infection: 211 with Omicron (temporal proxy), 424 with RSV, 824 with HRV, and 957 with other viruses. Primary outcomes were UAO and neurological events. Propensity score matching (1:2) compared Omicron with RSV and HRV, adjusting for age, sex, comorbidities, and admission severity. A natural-experiment analysis compared first exposure (Wave 1, December 2022–February 2023, n = 82) versus second exposure (Wave 2+, March–December 2023, n = 51) among children ≥ 6 months of age. Age-stratified and wave-period analyzes were prespecified. Results UAO occurred in 20 of 211 children with Omicron (9.5%, 95% CI 5.9–14.2%) versus 1 of 424 with RSV (0.2%) and 1 of 824 with HRV (0.2%). Any neurological event was observed in 44 of 211 with Omicron (20.9%, 95% CI 15.7–26.9%) versus 20 of 424 with RSV (4.7%) and 26 of 824 with HRV (3.2%). After matching, Omicron was associated with increased risks of MODS score ≥ 2 (vs. RSV: RR 3.80, 95% CI 1.84–7.86; vs. HRV: RR 4.50, 95% CI 2.32–8.72), non-febrile neurological events (vs. RSV: RR 5.2, 95% CI 2.8–9.6; vs. HRV: RR 6.8, 95% CI 3.9–11.8), and severe adverse outcomes (vs. RSV: RR 3.08, 95% CI 1.52–6.24; vs. HRV: RR 3.85, 95% CI 1.98–7.49). In the immune exposure analysis, severe outcomes were markedly lower after second exposure (13.7%) than after first exposure (45.1%; p < 0.001), representing a 71% relative reduction. UAO decreased from 18.3% to 2.0% (p = 0.005), while LRTI rates were unchanged (45.1% vs. 56.9%; p = 0.214), indicating immune “taming” of severity without prevention of infection. Conclusions Pediatric Omicron infection was associated with substantially higher rates of UAO and neurological events than RSV or HRV, with risks extending beyond infancy. Immune priming dramatically attenuated severe outcomes and upper airway toxicity, though lower respiratory involvement persisted. These findings document the transition of Omicron from a novel, severe pediatric pathogen toward an established respiratory virus, and highlight the need for age-specific clinical vigilance and ongoing surveillance.

papers.title: Impact of national RSV immunization programme on the epidemiology of bronchiolitis in Greece.
papers.abstract: Abstract Universal RSV immunization strategies for infants, including monoclonal antibody administration and maternal vaccination during pregnancy, were implemented in Greece for the first time during the 2025–2026 season. We conducted a prospective observational study of infants aged <12 months hospitalized with bronchiolitis at a quaternary paediatric hospital in Greece between November 2025 and April 2026. Bronchiolitis incidence was compared with that of the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons. Severity of bronchiolitis was assessed using the modified Tal score. Across the three seasons, 854 of 15246 admissions were due to bronchiolitis. The incidence decreased significantly in 2025–2026 to 42 per 1000 admissions, compared to 64 and 59 in 2024–2025 and 2023–2024, respectively. The 2025–2026 epidemic curve of bronchiolitis was flatter and more prolonged, with a delayed peak in March. Of 186 infants with bronchiolitis, 19.9% had received RSV immunization. Disease severity and oxygen requirements did not differ significantly between immunized and unimmunized infants, although unimmunized infants were older and had a trend towards higher complication rates. In conclusion, national RSV immunization was associated with reduced bronchiolitis hospitalizations and complications. However, the smaller-than-expected reduction in disease rates underscores the need to improve awareness, coverage, and timely immunization.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of the national RSV immunization programme on the epidemiology of bronchiolitis in Greece, addressing the need to understand how such interventions affect disease patterns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective observational study was conducted at a quaternary paediatric hospital in Greece, examining infants aged <12 months hospitalized with bronchiolitis between November 2025 and April 2026.
analysis.methods: Bronchiolitis incidence was compared across three seasons, and severity was assessed using the modified Tal score. Immunization status was recorded for infants admitted with bronchiolitis.
analysis.main_results: Across the three seasons, 854 of 15246 admissions were due to bronchiolitis. The incidence decreased significantly in 2025–2026 to 42 per 1000 admissions, compared to 64 and 59 in 2024–2025 and 2023–2024, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that national RSV immunization was associated with reduced bronchiolitis hospitalizations and complications, highlighting its potential impact on disease burden.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that RSV immunization could be a valuable tool in reducing the incidence and severity of bronchiolitis, informing future public health strategies and vaccine implementation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The smaller-than-expected reduction in disease rates indicates the need for improved awareness, coverage, and timely immunization, which may affect the strength of the observed association.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of the national RSV immunization programme on bronchiolitis epidemiology in Greece during the 2025–2026 season. A prospective observational study was conducted at a quaternary paediatric hospital, comparing bronchiolitis incidence across three seasons. The results showed a significant decrease in bronchiolitis admissions in 2025–2026 compared to previous years, with the epidemic curve being flatter and more prolonged. The authors interpreted this as an association between RSV immunization and reduced hospitalizations and complications. The findings suggest that immunization could be a valuable strategy for mitigating bronchiolitis burden. However, the smaller-than-expected reduction highlights the need for improved awareness and coverage. The evidence is moderate, as the study is observational and does not establish causality.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 2025-2026 年季节期间,希腊首次实施了婴儿 RSV 通用免疫策略,包括孕期单克隆抗体注射和母亲 疫苗接种。我们对2025年11月至2026年4月期间在希腊一家四级儿科医院住院使用毛细支气管炎的年龄<12个月的婴儿进行了一项前瞻性观察研究。将毛细支气管炎 毛细支气管炎与2023-2024年和2024-2025年季节进行了比较。使用修改后的 Tal 评分评估 毛细支气管炎 的严重程度。在这三个赛季中,15246 次入场中有 854 次是由于 毛细支气管炎 造成的。2025-2026 年,发病率 显着下降至每 1000 名入学者中有 42 名,而 2024-2025 年和 2023-2024 年分别为 64 名和 59 名。毛细支气管炎 2025-2026年流行曲线更平坦、持续时间更长,3月份出现延迟高峰。在 186 名 毛细支气管炎 婴儿中,19.9% 接受过 RSV 免疫接种。尽管未免疫婴儿年龄较大且并发症发生率较高,但免疫婴儿和未免疫婴儿之间的疾病严重程度和需氧量没有显着差异。总之,全国 RSV 免疫接种与 毛细支气管炎 住院率和并发症的减少相关。然而,疾病发病率下降幅度小于预期,凸显了提高认识、覆盖率和及时免疫接种的必要性。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,全国 RSV 免疫接种与 毛细支气管炎 住院率和并发症的减少相关,突显了其对疾病负担的潜在影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RSV 免疫可能是减少 发病率 和 毛细支气管炎 严重程度的宝贵工具,为未来的公共卫生策略和 疫苗 实施提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 疾病发病率下降幅度小于预期表明需要提高认识、覆盖范围和及时免疫接种,这可能会影响观察到的关联强度。

papers.title: Estimating viral interference from wastewater surveillance: a Bayesian multi-pathogen SEIR framework.
papers.abstract: The concurrent circulation of influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV creates complex transmission dynamics in which infection with one virus may reduce or enhance transmission of another. We developed a Bayesian multi-pathogen SEIR model in which the transmission of each virus is reduced by the prevalence of co-circulating pathogens, quantified by an aggregate population-level interference coefficient θ. We fit the model to weekly wastewater data from six Canadian provinces over the 2024-2025 respiratory season, avoiding the use of clinical data, which are limited by under-reporting and inconsistent testing. Our findings show the estimated interference corresponded to a 4 to 30% reduction in peak transmission of each virus during co-circulation, with smaller reductions in the effective reproduction number. Although these estimates are based on a single respiratory season and can vary under different patterns of co-circulation, they are consistent with recent studies on multi-pathogen viral interference using clinical surveillance data.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 2024-2025 年呼吸季节期间加拿大六个省份的废水数据,开发了贝叶斯多病原体 SEIR 模型,以量化在存在共循环病原体的情况下每种病毒的 传播 减少量。

papers.title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). METHODS: Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock-vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. RESULTS: We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV-vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV-specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. CONCLUSION: Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi-center preclinical vaccine studies.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在欧洲两个灵长类研究机构的一项随机、盲法、双中心研究中,我们评估了 DNA 初免口咽腺病毒增强 疫苗接种 策略针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的免疫原性和保护功效。方法:恒河猴通过电穿孔接收 RSV 融合蛋白 (F) DNA 疫苗,然后两次粘膜注射编码相同抗原的重组腺病毒 媒介。模拟接种动物和模拟原发性 RSV 感染诱导的自然免疫的比较组作为对照。纵向监测全身和粘膜免疫应答。结果:我们检测到了强大的细胞和体液 免疫应答,但两个中心之间存在一些差异。然而,接种 RSV 疫苗的动物在 RSV 攻击感染后,上呼吸道和下呼吸道中的病毒复制明显减少。一个研究中心的对照组中出现了意外的 RSV 特异性免疫,导致无法确认预定义的主要终点。结论:我们的结果支持 DNA 引发后粘膜腺病毒增强诱导针对 RSV 的保护性免疫的潜力,同时强调了与多中心临床前 疫苗 研究相关的挑战。

papers.title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Factors Associated With Nirsevimab Receipt Among Children Aged Younger Than 20 Months in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network in 2023 to 2025.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We aim to evaluate the association of sociodemographic and clinical factors with nirsevimab receipt among children with medically attended acute respiratory illness (ARI) across multiple seasons and beyond birth hospitalization. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We included nirsevimab-eligible children aged younger than 8 months and 8 to 19 months with ARI enrolled in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network during the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) seasons (October 1 to March 31). A mixed-effects logistic regression model was used to evaluate the association between sociodemographic and clinical factors with the likelihood of nirsevimab receipt among enrolled children aged younger than 8 months. RESULTS: Of the 2151 nirsevimab-eligible children with ARI enrolled in the 2023 to 2024 RSV season and 1819 in the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, 96% were aged younger than 8 months and in their first RSV season. Fourteen percent and 36% of eligible children aged younger than 8 months received nirsevimab in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 seasons, respectively. Among infants aged younger than 8 months, those born during the RSV season and those with an underlying medical condition were more likely to receive nirsevimab in both RSV seasons; infant female sex and maternal education were also associated with nirsevimab receipt during 2023 to 2024 but not 2024 to 2025. CONCLUSION: Most nirsevimab-eligible children with medically attended ARI in this analysis did not receive nirsevimab during the first 2 seasons of nirsevimab availability. Factors such as birth before the RSV season were associated with a decreased likelihood of nirsevimab receipt, emphasizing the need for tailored interventions following birth hospitalization to increase nirsevimab uptake for this group of children.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the factors associated with nirsevimab receipt among children with medically attended acute respiratory illness (ARI) during the first two seasons of its availability. The research focused on children aged younger than 20 months enrolled in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network during the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 RSV seasons. The study used a mixed-effects logistic regression model to analyze sociodemographic and clinical factors. Results showed that 14% and 36% of eligible children aged younger than 8 months received nirsevimab in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 seasons, respectively. The findings suggest potential strategies for increasing vaccine access and highlight the importance of considering birth timing and medical conditions in vaccination programs.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:我们的目的是评估社会人口统计学和临床​​因素与在多个季节和出生后住院治疗的急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 儿童中接受 尼塞韦单抗 的关系。患者和方法:我们纳入了在 2023 年至 2024 年和 2024 年至 2025 年 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 季节(10 月 1 日至 3 月 31 日)期间加入新 疫苗 监测 网络的符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格的儿童,年龄小于 8 个月和 8 至 19 个月。使用混合效应逻辑回归模型来评估社会人口统计学和临床​​因素与 8 个月以下入组儿童接受 尼塞韦单抗 的可能性之间的关联。结果:在 2023 年至 2024 年 RSV 季节登记的 2151 名符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格的 ARI 儿童和 2024 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节登记的 1819 名儿童中,96% 的年龄小于 8 个月且处于第一个 RSV 季节。在 2023 年至 2024 年和 2024 年至 2025 年季节,分别有 14% 和 36% 的 8 个月以下符合条件的儿童获得了 尼塞韦单抗。在 8 个月以下的婴儿中,在 RSV 季节出生的婴儿和有基础疾病的婴儿更有可能在两个 RSV 季节接受 尼塞韦单抗;婴儿女性性别和母亲教育也与 2023 年至 2024 年期间的 尼塞韦单抗 接收相关,但与 2024 年至 2025 年无关。结论:本次分析中,大多数符合 尼塞韦单抗 资格且就医的 ARI 儿童在 尼塞韦单抗 可用性的前 2 个季节期间没有接受 尼塞韦单抗。RSV 季节之前出生等因素与 尼塞韦单抗 接收的可能性降低相关,强调需要在出生住院后采取量身定制的干预措施,以增加该组儿童对 尼塞韦单抗 的吸收。

papers.title: Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has been applied for public health surveillance for several decades but gained unprecedented global prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to its broader adoption for multi-pathogen surveillance. However, the impact of heterogeneous urban wastewater infrastructure on the detection and interpretation of pathogen signals remains inadequately characterised, particularly in settings such as Mumbai, with fragmented and partially connected sewer networks. This study systematically compared multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance from centralised sewage treatment plants (STPs) and decentralised open drains (ODs), which represent aggregated and localised population catchments, respectively. Wastewater was collected during two monitoring periods (2023 and 2024) and analysed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Comparative analyses included detection frequency, temporal dynamics, and patterns of viral co-occurrence between node types. Viral detection rates were highest in STP influent, consistent with signal integration over larger populations and reduced short-term variability. Conversely, open drains exhibited greater temporal fluctuation, which may be consistent with localised, short-term changes but with reduced signal persistence. In the absence of concurrent clinical data, these node-level differences are interpreted as patterns in the wastewater signal rather than demonstrated gains in epidemiological sensitivity or earlier detection. SARS-CoV-2 was consistently detected across both node types, while influenza virus detection was more sporadic and exhibited marked variability, suggesting seasonal transmission dynamics. Co-detection of influenza A and B was observed in 2023, and influenza A subtyping revealed limited within-type diversity; source attribution for the detected subtypes could not be determined. Collectively, these findings indicate that wastewater signal profiles reflect an interplay between pathogen-specific characteristics and the structural configuration of the sampling network. papers.title: Prompt engineering for epidemiological surveillance: A step toward wider access to public health data analysis through natural language processing.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to describe and assess a framework that generates epidemiological analysis scripts from natural-language queries constrained by surveillance data dictionaries. STUDY DESIGN: Methodological framework development with internal consistency assessment. METHODS: PEFES (Prompt Engineering for Epidemiological Surveillance) restricts large language model output to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes, validates scope before generating a script, and does not execute code. Two authors with prior programming experience ('raters') submitted identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A and dengue) using Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.7 Flash against OpenDataSUS datasets. RESULTS: The two raters agreed on the behavior for all 22 scope-control queries: the 17 queries that were expected to be declined did not produce a script, and all 5 in-scope counterparts produced a script. Every source field read was dictionary-declared. Reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries and divergent for 8 (all where a prompt left a choice unstated). One session compared a declared field against wrong-type values, returning empty tables under formatted headings. CONCLUSIONS: Dictionary constraints restricted which data a generated script could analyze, but not how it was analyzed: reproducibility was dependent on both the prompt and dictionary, not the constraint mechanism alone. Errors within the declared set were identified by rater review, not by the framework, motivating pre-execution type checks or returning unstated choices as clarification requests. PEFES accelerates epidemiological work rather than replacing it, and it is a step toward wider access to surveillance data analysis.

METHODS: PEFES (Prompt Engineering for Epidemiological Surveillance) restricts large language model output to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes, validates scope before generating a script, and does not execute code. Two authors with prior programming experience ('raters') submitted identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A and dengue) using Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.7 Flash against OpenDataSUS datasets. RESULTS: The two raters agreed on the behavior for all 22 scope-control queries: the 17 queries that were expected to be declined did not produce a script, and all 5 in-scope counterparts produced a script. Every source field read was dictionary-declared. Reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries and divergent for 8 (all where a prompt left a choice unstated). One session compared a declared field against wrong-type values, returning empty tables under formatted headings. CONCLUSIONS: Dictionary constraints restricted which data a generated script could analyze, but not how it was analyzed: reproducibility was dependent on both the prompt and dictionary, not the constraint mechanism alone. Errors within the declared set were identified by rater review, not by the framework, motivating pre-execution type checks or returning unstated choices as clarification requests. PEFES accelerates epidemiological work rather than replacing it, and it is a step toward wider access to surveillance data analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces PEFES, a framework that generates epidemiological analysis scripts from natural-language queries constrained by surveillance data dictionaries. The aim was to assess the framework's ability to restrict data analysis to dictionary-declared variables and coding schemes. The study involved two authors with programming experience submitting identical sets of 22 in-scope and 22 scope-control queries across three case studies (respiratory syncytial virus, influenza A, and dengue) using large language models against OpenDataSUS datasets. The results showed that all 17 scope-control queries were declined, while all 5 in-scope queries produced scripts. Every source field read was dictionary-declared, and reported values were identical for 14 of the 22 in-scope queries. The authors concluded that dictionary constraints limit data analysis scope but not the analysis method itself, with reproducibility depending on both the prompt and dictionary. The framework's potential to accelerate epidemiological work and improve access to surveillance data analysis is highlighted, though the study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on internal consistency assessment and limited case studies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述和评估一个框架,该框架根据 监测 数据字典约束的自然语言查询生成流行病学分析脚本。该框架的开发是为了满足对更易于使用的公共卫生数据分析工具的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及开发具有内部一致性评估的方法框架。两位具有编程经验的作者使用 Claude Opus 4.8 和 Gemini 3.7 Flash 针对 OpenDataSUS 数据集在三个案例研究(呼吸道合胞病毒、甲型流感和登革热)中提交了相同的 22 个范围内查询和 22 个范围控制查询集。
elements_zh.methods: PEFES(流行病学提示工程 监测)将大型语言模型输出限制为字典声明的变量和编码方案,在生成脚本之前验证范围,并且不执行代码。通过将生成的脚本与预定义的查询和数据集进行比较来测试该框架。
elements_zh.main_results: 两位评估者就所有 22 个范围控制查询的行为达成一致:预计被拒绝的 17 个查询没有生成脚本,而所有 5 个范围内对应查询都生成了脚本。读取的每个源字段都是字典声明的。22 个范围内查询中,有 14 个查询的报告值相同,有 8 个查询的报告值不同(所有查询均在提示中留下了未说明的选项)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 字典约束限制了生成的脚本可以分析哪些数据,但不限制如何分析数据:可重复性取决于提示和字典,而不仅仅是约束机制。该研究强调了自然语言处理在流行病学领域的潜力 监测。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: PEFES 加速了流行病学工作,而不是取代它,这是朝着更广泛地获取 监测 数据分析迈出的一步。这可以提高公共卫生数据处理和解释的效率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 声明的集合中的错误是由评估者审查而不是由框架识别的,从而激发执行前类型检查或返回未声明的选择作为澄清请求。由于该研究是基于内部一致性评估和有限的案例研究,因此证据是中等的。

papers.title: First- and Second-Year Outcomes After Nirsevimab Immunization.
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The consistency of nirsevimab effectiveness across consecutive seasons and its broader clinical protective effects remain to be fully characterized. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether first-season effectiveness of nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI)-related hospitalizations is maintained during a new RSV season, whether the effectiveness persists beyond the first season, and whether nirsevimab exposure is associated with hospitalizations for non-RSV infections and asthma during the first and second years of follow-up. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed 2 nationwide matched cohorts using the French National Health Data System, including infants born in metropolitan France before the 2023 and 2024 immunization campaigns. Infants receiving nirsevimab were matched 1:1 to unimmunized infants. Both cohorts were followed up for 1 year after immunization, with an additional second year of follow-up for the 2023 cohort. Data analysis was performed from February 2023 to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Single dose of nirsevimab. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: RSV-LRTI-related, non-RSV infection, and asthma hospitalizations were assessed using weighted Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: This cohort study included 74 672 infants in 2023 and 175 526 in 2024. At baseline, the mean (SD) age of immunized infants was 4.5 (2.0) months in the 2023 cohort; 19 633 (52.6%) were male and 17 703 (47.4%) were female. The mean (SD) age of the 2024 cohort was 4.8 (2.2) months; 44 863 immunized infants (51.1%) were male and 42 900 (48.9%) were female. Among 37 366 infant pairs in 2023 and 87 763 pairs in 2024, RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year of follow-up occurred in 299 (0.8%) immunized vs 899 (2.4%) unimmunized infants in 2023 and 456 (0.5%) vs 1711 (1.9%), respectively, in 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with a lower rate of RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization in both the 2023 and 2024 cohort during the first year of follow-up, with effectiveness estimates of 66% (95% CI, 61%-70%) and 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%), respectively. An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ear, nose, and throat (ENT) bacterial infections was observed (2023 cohort: weighted hazard ratio [wHR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.84; 2024 cohort: wHR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.15-1.78). No significant association was observed for other outcomes. During the second year of follow-up, no protective association was observed for RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization (wHR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.73-1.43). An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ENT (wHR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.10-2.22) and asthma (wHR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.05-1.46) was observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that nirsevimab was associated with a substantial reduction in RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year across both the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 seasons. It was not associated with reduced hospitalizations due to non-RSV infections or asthma, nor during the second year of follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of nirsevimab against RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations and its association with non-RSV infections and asthma in infants during the first and second years of follow-up. The research aimed to determine if the first-season effectiveness of nirsevimab was maintained in subsequent seasons and whether its exposure was linked to hospitalizations for other conditions. The study used two nationwide matched cohorts from the French National Health Data System, analyzing data from February 2023 to August 2025. Results showed that nirsevimab was associated with a substantial reduction in RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year, with effectiveness estimates of 66% and 72% in the 2023 and 2024 cohorts, respectively. However, no protective association was observed during the second year, and higher rates of ENT bacterial infections and asthma were noted. The authors concluded that while nirsevimab provides significant short-term protection against RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations, its long-term efficacy and impact on other conditions require further investigation. The study's findings have implications for RSV vaccination strategies but are limited by observational design and potential confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 尼塞韦单抗 在连续季节中对 RSV-LRTI 相关住院治疗的有效性,及其与随访第一年和第二年因非 RSV 感染和哮喘住院的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项 队列研究 研究使用法国国家健康数据系统分析了 2 个全国匹配的 队列研究,其中包括 2023 年和 2024 年免疫接种活动之前在法国本土出生的婴儿。接受 尼塞韦单抗 的婴儿与未免疫婴儿以 1:1 进行匹配。两种 队列研究 均在免疫后随访 1 年,并对 2023 队列研究 进行第二年随访。
elements_zh.methods: 使用加权 Cox 比例风险模型评估 RSV-LRTI 相关、非 RSV 感染和哮喘住院情况。数据分析于2023年2月至2025年8月进行。
elements_zh.main_results: Among 37 366 infant pairs in 2023 and 87 763 pairs in 2024, RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year of follow-up occurred in 299 (0.8%) immunized vs 899 (2.4%) unimmunized infants in 2023 and 456 (0.5%) vs 1711 (1.9%), respectively, in 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with a lower rate of RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization in both the 2023 and 2024 cohort during the first year of follow-up, with effectiveness estimates of 66% (95% CI, 61%-70%) and 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%), respectively. An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ENT bacterial infections was observed (2023 cohort: weighted hazard ratio [wHR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.84; 2024 cohort: wHR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.15-1.78).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,尼塞韦单抗 与 2023-2024 年和 2024-2025 年季节第一年 RSV-LRTI 相关住院治疗的大幅减少有关。然而,他们指出,这与非 RSV 感染或哮喘导致的住院治疗减少无关,也与随访第二年的减少无关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,尼塞韦单抗 可能在免疫后第一年针对 RSV-LRTI 相关住院提供显着保护,这可以为未来针对婴儿 RSV 的 疫苗接种 策略提供信息。然而,第二年缺乏保护性关联以及与非 RSV 感染或哮喘的关联表明需要进一步研究以了解长期影响和更广泛的影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖于国家卫生数据系统的观察数据而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差或混杂因素。由于缺乏随机对照试验以及数据收集和随访方面的潜在限制,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 尼塞韦单抗 免疫后第一年和第二年的结果。
papers.source_body_en: IMPORTANCE: The consistency of nirsevimab effectiveness across consecutive seasons and its broader clinical protective effects remain to be fully characterized. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether first-season effectiveness of nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI)-related hospitalizations is maintained during a new RSV season, whether the effectiveness persists beyond the first season, and whether nirsevimab exposure is associated with hospitalizations for non-RSV infections and asthma during the first and second years of follow-up. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study analyzed 2 nationwide matched cohorts using the French National Health Data System, including infants born in metropolitan France before the 2023 and 2024 immunization campaigns. Infants receiving nirsevimab were matched 1:1 to unimmunized infants. Both cohorts were followed up for 1 year after immunization, with an additional second year of follow-up for the 2023 cohort. Data analysis was performed from February 2023 to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Single dose of nirsevimab. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: RSV-LRTI-related, non-RSV infection, and asthma hospitalizations were assessed using weighted Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: This cohort study included 74 672 infants in 2023 and 175 526 in 2024. At baseline, the mean (SD) age of immunized infants was 4.5 (2.0) months in the 2023 cohort; 19 633 (52.6%) were male and 17 703 (47.4%) were female. The mean (SD) age of the 2024 cohort was 4.8 (2.2) months; 44 863 immunized infants (51.1%) were male and 42 900 (48.9%) were female. Among 37 366 infant pairs in 2023 and 87 763 pairs in 2024, RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year of follow-up occurred in 299 (0.8%) immunized vs 899 (2.4%) unimmunized infants in 2023 and 456 (0.5%) vs 1711 (1.9%), respectively, in 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with a lower rate of RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization in both the 2023 and 2024 cohort during the first year of follow-up, with effectiveness estimates of 66% (95% CI, 61%-70%) and 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%), respectively. An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ear, nose, and throat (ENT) bacterial infections was observed (2023 cohort: weighted hazard ratio [wHR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.84; 2024 cohort: wHR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.15-1.78). No significant association was observed for other outcomes. During the second year of follow-up, no protective association was observed for RSV-LRTI-related hospitalization (wHR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.73-1.43). An association with higher rates of hospitalization for ENT (wHR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.10-2.22) and asthma (wHR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.05-1.46) was observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that nirsevimab was associated with a substantial reduction in RSV-LRTI-related hospitalizations during the first year across both the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 seasons. It was not associated with reduced hospitalizations due to non-RSV infections or asthma, nor during the second year of follow-up.

papers.title: The Impact of Socioeconomic and Geographic Factors in Respiratory Virus Testing in Australia.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes significant disease burden in Australia, yet most confirmatory laboratory data come from acute healthcare settings. This study analyses RSV and other respiratory virus testing across different socio-demographic groups and healthcare settings using data from private and public laboratories Australia-wide. METHODOLOGY: We analysed de-identified nucleic acid amplification test (NAATs) data for RSV (n=9.35 million), influenza A (n=9.42 million), influenza B (n=9.26 million), and SARS-CoV-2 (n=52.94 million) from 1 September 2017 to 31 August 2023, sourced from the three largest private and two public pathology providers in Australia. Data were stratified by socio-economic indexes for areas (SEIFA), remoteness, age, jurisdiction and care settings. Population-adjusted testing rates and positivity percentages were calculated. RESULTS: NAATs were highest in the most advantaged socio-economic quintile and major cities, declining with increased socio-economic disadvantage and geographic remoteness. Positivity rates were highest in the most advantaged quintile, but no consistent pattern was seen across other quintiles. Community settings accounted for most RSV testing, predominantly by private pathology providers. The COVID-19 pandemic from 2020 altered NAAT panels used and disrupted usual seasonal trends for RSV and influenza. CONCLUSION: Substantial variation exists in respiratory virus NAAT and positivity rates across socio-demographic groups, jurisdictions, and healthcare settings. Improving equitable access to testing among disadvantaged and remote populations is essential for accurate surveillance, timely intervention and effective prioritisation of public health interventions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决澳大利亚不同社会经济和地理环境中呼吸道病毒检测模式的巨大差距,重点关注呼吸道合胞病毒和其他呼吸道病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了 2017 年 9 月 1 日至 2023 年 8 月 31 日期间 RSV、甲型流感、乙型流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的去识别化核酸扩增测试 (NAAT) 数据,这些数据来自澳大利亚三个最大的私人和两个公共病理学提供商,涉及各种社会经济指标、偏远地区、年龄、管辖范围和护理环境。
elements_zh.methods: RSV、甲型流感、乙型流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的 NAAT 数据按地区社会经济指数 (SEIFA)、偏远程度、年龄、管辖范围和护理环境进行分层,并计算了人口调整后的检测率和阳性百分比。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV NAAT 在最有利的社会经济五分位和主要城市中最高,随着社会经济劣势和地理偏远的增加而下降。最有利的五分之一的阳性率最高,但在其他五分之一中没有看到一致的模式。社区环境占 RSV 检测的大部分,主要由私人病理学提供者进行。COVID-19 大流行改变了 NAAT 检测组的使用,并扰乱了 RSV 和流感的通常季节性趋势。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,不同社会人口群体、司法管辖区和医疗机构的呼吸道病毒 NAAT 和阳性率存在显着差异,这凸显了弱势群体和偏远人群公平获得检测机会的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 改善弱势和偏远人群获得检测的公平机会对于准确的 监测、及时干预和有效确定公共卫生干预措施的优先顺序至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果受到对去识别化数据的依赖以及测试模式可能存在偏差的限制。样本量和数据来源很全面,但可能无法完全代表澳大利亚的所有社会经济和地理区域。
